confirmed.title: appendResult loads every image of a sweep at full resolution, uncapped
confirmed.description: `appendResult` builds the viewer's `` with `img.src = rec.url` - the full-resolution PNG under `/outputs` - and, unlike the gallery card (app.js:599) and the sheet cell (app.js:926), sets no `loading` attribute. Nothing trims the strip either: `clearResults()` runs only on the first image of a new job, so the viewer accumulates one eagerly-fetched full-res `` per image the job produces - up to 512 for a plain request (runs 64 x num_images 8) and up to `settings.max_grid_images` = 1024 for a grid. `.viewer.many img { max-height: 20vh }` shrinks the display box, not the download or the decode. The reattach path is a sharper burst: `events()` opens with a snapshot carrying every image made so far, and `onmessage` does `data.images.forEach(show)`, so a reload at cell 900 appends 900 eager full-res images in one synchronous pass.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Leave the page open on the flagship use case - a 1024-cell overnight grid at the 4 MP tier. Measured with Pillow at the code's own compress_level=4, a representative 2048x2048 output is 5.08 MB encoded and 16.8 MB decoded, so the tab fetches ~5.2 GB over loopback and holds 1024 live img elements; the 1 MP tier is still ~1.4 GB. The renderer's memory climbs all night, the tab becomes unresponsive or is killed, and the fetches contend for the same disk the generation thread is writing the next PNG to. Reloading mid-grid queues 900 fetches at once, six at a time over uvicorn's HTTP/1.1.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Two lines and a cap in `appendResult`: `img.loading = 'lazy'; img.decoding = 'async';` and `while (els.viewer.children.length > VIEWER_MAX) els.viewer.firstElementChild.remove();` with VIEWER_MAX 24-48. Keep pushing every record into `viewerRecords` so the lightbox still walks the whole run, and put any '... and N more this run' note outside `#viewer` (the cap loop and `clearResults()`'s innerHTML wipe would otherwise eat it). Lazy alone is not enough: `.viewer img` sets no height, so unloaded images stack inside the viewport and all become eligible immediately - the DOM cap does the work. Pairs with the thumbnail derivative filed separately.

confirmed.title: renderSheet crosses two unbounded axes and rescans all records per cell, so the Sheet button freezes the tab on an unfiltered gallery
confirmed.description: `renderSheet` lays out `colValues.length x rowValues.length` cells, where each axis is the distinct values the loaded records take, and for every cell runs `sheetRecords.find((r) => matches(r, rowValue, colValue))` over up to 1024 records. Nothing caps the product. Seeds are unique per image by construction, so `values.seed.length` equals the page size for any set that is not one grid's seed axis, and `chooseAxes` sorts by distinct count descending - so seed always wins the columns slot on a mixed gallery. The constant factor compounds it: `matches` allocates `Object.entries(sheetAxes.pins)` and calls `axisByKey` - itself a `SHEET_AXES.find` - up to five times per record per cell. The trigger is the invited action, not a corner case: the Sheet button with the search box empty, whose title reads 'Arrange these images by their settings'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Running the verbatim SHEET_AXES/sheetValues/chooseAxes/matches/cell-loop code under Node 24 against 1024 synthetic records: 60 distinct prompts gives cols=seed(1024) x rows=prompt(60) = 61,440 cells and 1.55 s of matching alone for 171 non-empty cells; 400 distinct prompts gives 409,600 cells and 9.97 s. That is JIT-warmed JS with no DOM; on top of it the loop appends 61,440-409,600 divs and sets gridTemplateColumns to `auto repeat(1024, minmax(96px, 1fr))`, a grid at least 100,000 px wide. The escape route re-triggers it: the search box debounces `resetGallery` at 250 ms and each reset in sheet mode is a fresh 1024-row fetch plus a full renderSheet, so typing the `job:` filter that would fix the layout costs another freeze per pause.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Any one of three defuses it, and all three are worth having: (1) refuse rather than render past ~4096 cells, with a note telling the user to filter to one run; (2) index instead of scanning - one pass into a Map keyed by row and column value, turning O(cells x records) into O(records + cells); (3) hoist the pins and axisByKey lookups out of `matches`. Also make `chooseAxes` skip an axis whose distinct count equals `records.length` - an axis with one value per image is a list, not a dimension.

confirmed.title: A browser grid's drawn base seed is published nowhere, and the documented recovery resumes onto the wrong seed window
confirmed.description: `grid.expand()` draws the base seed itself when the request has none, and every cell then carries a derived seed, `wrap_seed(base + index * num_images)`. The base is never surfaced: `/api/grid` returns only `JobAccepted(job_id=...)`, `Job.snapshot()` has no seed field, the per-cell label is steps/CFG/mu, and `web/app.js` never writes anything back into the Seed box after a submit. Resume is nevertheless refused without an explicit seed, so the base seed is the one thing a resumed night cannot do without. All three places that tell the user how to recover it give the same wrong instruction - `web/index.html:179`, `README.md:296` and the 422 body at `backend/schemas.py:102` all say 'reuse any image of that run', which is correct only for seeds == 1. The gallery is ordered `id DESC`, so the image nearest to hand is the newest: the highest seed the night reached, not the base.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Run against the repo's own code (steps_axis '6,8', cfg_axis '1,2', seeds 4, base 1000, night dies after 2 seeds). With num_images=1, resuming from the newest image (seed 1001) expands to seeds 1001..1004 and renders 1002, 1003 and 1004 - a seed the grid never contained - 12 cells instead of the 8 outstanding. With num_images=2 (cell seeds 1000, 1002, 1004, 1006; saved image seeds 1000..1003), resuming from the newest image (seed 1003) expands to cell seeds 1003, 1005, 1007, 1009 - disjoint from the original: prune_done drops 4 of 16, renders 12 cells at seeds that answer no question, and the grid's own remaining seeds 1004 and 1006 are never rendered. The only way to get the true base today is to filter `job:<id>` and page to the oldest row - 22 clicks of 'Load more' for 1024 images. The CLI has none of this problem: generate.py prints the drawn seed before the run.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Publish the base seed and let the panel keep it. Add `seed` to `Job.snapshot()` and to `JobAccepted` (`run_grid` already has `cells` in hand, so `JobAccepted(job_id=job.id, seed=cells[0].seed)` is one line; `submit()` should do the same for a plain sweep). In `startJob()`, write it into an empty Seed box after the POST. Include it in `/api/jobs` rows. Fix the instruction in all three copies to say the first/oldest image, and note that with batch > 1 only the first image of a batch carries a cell's seed. Optionally 422 a resume whose seed matches no cell_key in `completed_cells()`. CLAUDE.md's resume bullet and its 'reuse it from any image' corollary are the passage that has to change: keying on settings is right, but the seed is the one setting the client is never given back.

confirmed.title: The prompt axis's cartesian product is materialised before any ceiling is checked, on the event loop
confirmed.description: `prompt_assignments()` builds the entire product of the prompt variables as a real list of dicts before anything counts it. `MAX_AXIS_VALUES = 64` caps values per variable, never the number of variables or their product, and the only whole-grid ceiling (`total * num_images > settings.max_grid_images`) is computed from `len(assignments)` - a number that exists only once the list has been built. `main._expand` makes it worse: it calls `grid.axis_values(...)` and then `grid.expand(...)`, and each calls `prompt_assignments()`, so the product is materialised two or three times per request. Both `/api/grid` and `/api/grid/preview` are `async def` calling `_expand` inline, so all of it runs on the event loop - in contrast to `storage.step_cost_ms` two lines later, which is correctly wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `GridRequest.prompt_axis` allows 2000 characters and a variable line costs ~7, so ~280 binary variables fit. Measured on this checkout: 18 variables (287 chars) = 262,144 assignments in 1.14-1.38 s; 20 variables = 1,048,576 in 3.06 s at 743 MB peak (tracemalloc); 22 variables = 4,194,304 in ~2.9 s for the dicts alone; 4 variables x 32 values took 0.90 s and 208 MB to build then 7.28 s and 271 MB to substitute. Through HTTP an 18-variable axis blocked for 1.38 s and then answered 422 'past the 1024 a grid may queue'. The UI fires `/api/grid/preview` on a 250 ms debounce from every keystroke in the prompt-variables textarea, so typing or pasting a block walks the product up one doubling at a time, and because it is the event loop the freeze is server-wide: SSE progress stops, `/api/status` stalls, and `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel` cannot be served - so an overnight sweep running at the time cannot be stopped, and a MemoryError takes it down with the process.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Count the product before building it, in `prompt_assignments` after the placeholder checks: `count = math.prod(len(v) for v in variables.values())` and raise ValueError past `settings.max_grid_images` - `grid.py` already imports `settings`, and `_expand`'s existing except-ValueError-to-422 needs no change. `expand()`'s own guard then only ever sees a bounded `len(assignments)`. While there, have `main._expand` pass the already-resolved axes into `expand()` instead of resolving them twice, and consider `await asyncio.to_thread(_expand, request)` in both grid endpoints so a large-but-legal grid cannot stall the loop either.

confirmed.title: `_shifts_itself` treats 'not dynamic' as 'no shift', so the fallback composes with the scheduler's static shift into mu + ln(shift)
confirmed.description: `_shifts_itself()` answers only `scheduler.config.use_dynamic_shifting`. When that is False the backend pre-shifts the ramp itself with `_shifted_sigmas(steps, mu)` and blanks mu. But `use_dynamic_shifting: false` does not mean no shift: `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler.set_timesteps` is an if/else, and the else branch applies `sigmas = self.shift * sigmas / (1 + (self.shift - 1) * sigmas)` - which multiplies the odds s/(1-s) by `shift`, exactly as the exponential branch multiplies them by e^mu. The two compose into an effective mu of `mu + ln(shift)`: the same additive composition as the 2026-08-29 review's top finding, surviving inside the branch written as its fix. `_shifted_sigmas`'s docstring claims it is safe because it is 'only used for a scheduler that does not shift on its own', which is true only when shift == 1.0 - and tests/test_schedule.py:109 passes exactly `shift=1.0`, the one value that makes the static branch the identity, so the only test covering this branch passes whether the backend compensates or not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driving `DiffusersBackend.generate()` through the repo's own StubPipeline with `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler(use_dynamic_shifting=False, shift=3.0)` and mu=1.15, the landed sigmas are [1.0, 0.9851, 0.9660, 0.9404, 0.9045, 0.8504, 0.7595, 0.5751] against the intended [1.0, 0.9567, 0.9045, 0.8403, 0.7595, 0.6546, 0.5128, 0.3109] - matching `_shifted_sigmas(8, 1.15 + ln 3)` to 1e-5. Reachable on any checkpoint with `use_dynamic_shifting: false` and shift != 1.0 (SD3/3.5 ship shift 3.0, Lumina 2 ships 6.0), which launch.py's 'another repo id' option and the module docstring's 'any other diffusers text-to-image repo' both invite. Every image then runs at an effective 2.25 while ImageRecord.mu records 1.15, so Reuse reproduces the same wrong schedule and a mu sweep compares points that are all offset by ln(shift). The three catalogue families all set use_dynamic_shifting true and are unaffected.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Subtract the shift the scheduler will apply anyway, the same way `_forced_mu` replaces the mu the pipeline would have derived: read `shift` off the scheduler instance (set_timesteps uses `self.shift`, not `self.config.shift`) and pass `self._shifted_sigmas(request.steps, mu - math.log(shift))`. At shift == 1.0 that is byte-identical to today. Parametrize `test_a_scheduler_that_does_not_shift_gets_an_explicit_schedule` over shift in (1.0, 3.0) asserting `_applied(scheduler) == _schedule(mu)` - it fails today at 3.0 - and drop its `assert pipe.sigmas_arg == ...` line, which asserts the list the backend computed, exactly what CLAUDE.md says not to assert on. Correct the CLAUDE.md bullet: a non-dynamic scheduler still shifts, statically. While there, `shift_terminal`, `use_karras_sigmas`, `use_exponential_sigmas` and `use_beta_sigmas` also post-process the schedule in both branches; a warning when any is set would stop mu quietly meaning something else again.

confirmed.title: Ctrl-C cannot stop a running sweep: the cooperative cancel is in lifespan, which uvicorn runs only after draining the SSE connection
confirmed.description: `jobs.shutdown()` is the only thing that sets `cancel_requested` at exit, and it is called from the lifespan shutdown. uvicorn runs lifespan shutdown last: `Server.shutdown()` first calls `connection.shutdown()` on every open connection - which for an in-flight response only sets `keep_alive = False`, it does not close the transport - then awaits `_wait_tasks_to_complete()` with `timeout_graceful_shutdown`, which `main.run()` never passes and which defaults to None, i.e. unbounded. That wait spins while `server_state.connections` is non-empty, and the browser's EventSource connection will not complete until `jobs.events()` yields `done`, which only happens when the job finishes. So the cancel that is supposed to stop the sweep is queued behind the sweep. A second Ctrl-C sets `force_exit`, which breaks the wait but skips the lifespan call entirely - `jobs.shutdown()` and `backend.unload()` never run - and `serve()` then returns with a non-default ThreadPoolExecutor still executing `_generate`, which `concurrent.futures.thread._python_exit` joins at interpreter shutdown; `_generate` is one work item covering all of the job's cells, so the join waits for the entire remaining grid.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Start a 1024-cell grid with the browser tab open and press Ctrl-C. The log prints 'Shutting down' then 'Waiting for connections to close. (CTRL+C to force quit)' and sits there for the rest of the grid - hours - because the SSE stream is the connection it is waiting on and the job that would end that stream is never told to stop. Press Ctrl-C again: uvicorn stops waiting, skips lifespan, and the process then blocks in the atexit join on the gen thread, still denoising with cancel_requested False. Neither keystroke stops anything. With no browser attached the documented behaviour works, which is why this survives casual testing. The docstring at jobs.py:120 claims this path prevents exactly the hang it cannot reach.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Set the cancel flag on the signal, before uvicorn starts draining, instead of in lifespan: subclass `uvicorn.Server`, override `handle_exit` to set `job.cancel_requested = True` for every `jobs.active()` job and then call super(). The flag is then set on both the first and the forced Ctrl-C, so the worker unwinds within one step, `_run` emits `done`, the stream returns, the connection closes, and the normal drain completes. Pass `timeout_graceful_shutdown=30` as belt and braces for a client that stops reading, and keep `jobs.shutdown()` in lifespan as the join.

confirmed.title: Ctrl-C during a model load freezes the event loop until the load finishes: lifespan's backend.unload() blocks on the loader's lock
confirmed.description: `lifespan` calls `backend.unload()` synchronously on the event loop, not through `asyncio.to_thread` the way `unload_model()` does. `DiffusersBackend.unload()` opens with `with self._lock:` before the `if self._pipe is None: return` check, and `load()` holds that same `threading.Lock` for its entire body - from_pretrained, the offload wiring, everything. So during a load, shutdown blocks the loop inside a C-level lock acquire purely to discover there is nothing to unload. A second Ctrl-C cannot rescue it: uvicorn gates the lifespan call on `if not self.force_exit:`, a check that has already passed, and `handle_exit` only sets a flag nothing will read because the loop is not running. `jobs.shutdown()` provides no cover - a job blocked in `await self._ensure_loaded()` has never been submitted to `_pool`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `KREA_PRELOAD=true`, server started, no browser open (also reachable via `curl -X POST /api/model/load`, which returns instantly and closes, or by closing the tab during a load). Four minutes into the checkpoint download the user realises it is the wrong repo and presses Ctrl-C. uvicorn logs 'Shutting down' and the process then does nothing - no further log lines, no prompt returned - until the whole multi-GB load completes, which per CLAUDE.md's note about the xet downloader stalling a 12 GB checkpoint is not bounded. Repeated Ctrl-C has no effect; the only way out is killing the process, which risks leaving an uncollectable `<name>.png.part` if a save was in flight.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not block the loop, and do not fight the loader for the lock at shutdown - the process is exiting, so freeing VRAM buys nothing. At minimum `await asyncio.to_thread(backend.unload)`, matching main.py:179. Better, add a `try_unload()` that uses `self._lock.acquire(blocking=False)` and returns immediately if the loader holds it, and call that from lifespan. Independently, give `load()` a way to be abandoned (a `threading.Event` checked between component loads) so 'stop this load' is expressible at all.

confirmed.title: A gallery reset that lands while a page is in flight is silently dropped and never re-issued
confirmed.description: `resetGallery()` bumps `galleryEpoch`, zeroes `offset`, drops `galleryRecords`, empties the grid, and then calls `loadGallery()`. `loadGallery()` opens with `if (galleryPending) return galleryPending;` - so when a page is already in flight it starts no new fetch and hands back the old promise, which carries the pre-reset epoch and therefore discards itself at the epoch check. Both the stale response and the fresh query are lost: DOM cleared, records cleared, offset 0, no request outstanding, no retry scheduled, and `total`, `els.count`, `els.more.hidden` and `renderSheet()` all skipped. Nothing anywhere re-runs `loadGallery` afterwards. This is the previous review's `web/app.js:325` entry, fixed in 63c94b3 along the shape the review itself recommended - the fix cures the double-append and introduces this hole.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Transcribing lines 540-587 verbatim with the DOM stubbed and a 100 ms server: after a successful first load (48 cards, offset 48), two `resetGallery()` calls 20 ms apart leave 0 cards, offset 0, galleryPending null. Reachable by one gesture in four places: toggling Favorites twice during a load; typing across two 250 ms debounce ticks when the FTS query is slower than 250 ms (an empty gallery reading '(200)' - a false 'no results'); clicking a card's sheet button while a search timer is pending, which leaves the contact sheet blank and, because `els.more` is hidden in sheet mode, with no control that re-triggers a load; and the stream's `done` handler resetting while a 'Load more' page is in flight, so a night's output silently never appears.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Re-issue after the superseded request settles instead of sharing it. Either chain in `resetGallery`: `const pending = galleryPending; return pending ? pending.then(loadGallery) : loadGallery();` - the `.finally` that nulls `galleryPending` was attached at creation, so it runs first and the chained call finds a free slot - or re-issue from `loadGallery`'s own `finally` when the epoch has moved. Add a regression test at the seam the previous fix created: reset twice inside one fetch and assert a second request is issued.

confirmed.title: The lightbox can only be opened by clicking an , so it is unreachable by keyboard
confirmed.description: Every route into the lightbox is a click handler bound to a bare ``: app.js:534 (viewer), 600 (gallery card) and 930 (contact-sheet cell). An img is not in the tab order and fires no click on Enter/Space. `grep -n tabindex web/app.js` returns nothing and the same grep over index.html returns only the ten `.help` badges, so no image anywhere on the page is focusable, and the document keydown handler returns immediately while `els.lightbox.hidden` is true. This is the previous review's `app.js:312` accessibility-cluster entry, unfixed; the commits since only added a third click-only trigger, the sheet cell.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A keyboard-only user can tab to the search box, the favourites checkbox, the Sheet button and the (invisible) card tool buttons, but can never open a single image. That loses full-size viewing entirely, plus everything only the lightbox shows: the per-image metadata line (model, size, steps, CFG, mu, seed, duration) and prev/next navigation over a run. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard, level A) failure on the application's primary content interaction.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the trigger a real control. Cheapest: factor the three identical img builders into one `thumb(rec, list)` helper that sets `tabIndex = 0`, `role='button'`, an aria-label from the prompt, and a keydown handler for Enter/Space. Cleaner: wrap the image in a `<button class="thumb">` styled `all: unset`, which gives Enter, Space and a focus ring for free. Either way add a visible `:focus-visible` ring - the card's `.tools` opacity trick means UA outlines on card children are currently painted at opacity 0.

confirmed.title: Four storage calls run synchronous SQLite on the event loop, one of them taking a lock the generation thread holds
confirmed.description: `favorite`, `delete`, `gallery` and `_expand`'s resume lookup call into `storage` directly from `async def` handlers. `set_favorite` and `delete_image` do `with _write_lock, _session() as conn:` - `_write_lock` is the module-level `threading.Lock` the generation thread holds inside `save_image` for the length of its INSERT, and `_session()` connects with `timeout=15`, i.e. it will sit on SQLite's busy handler for fifteen seconds before giving up. This is not house style: the same file deliberately pushes `backend.describe`, `backend.unload` and `storage.step_cost_ms` onto `asyncio.to_thread`, with a comment saying why. `completed_cells` is the slowest of the four - up to three chunked scans over width/height/model_id with a 400-parameter prompt IN clause and no covering index - and it runs from `POST /api/grid/preview`, which the UI fires 250 ms after every keystroke in the grid panel.
confirmed.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md and clear.py's docstring both say `python -m backend.clear` is safe to run while the server is up. Do that during a sweep on a large gallery: `clear_history` holds SQLite's write lock across `DELETE FROM images` with the FTS5 trigger firing per row, and `vacuum()` then takes an exclusive lock. Clicking the heart on a card in that window blocks the event loop thread - first on `_write_lock` behind the generation thread's stalled INSERT, then on SQLite's busy handler - for up to 15 seconds, after which the handler raises OperationalError as a 500. For those seconds no SSE progress is delivered, `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel` does not execute, and `/api/status` does not answer. Milder everyday version: with Resume ticked and 50k rows, each keystroke in the grid prompt box stalls the loop for three unindexed table scans.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap all four in `asyncio.to_thread`, matching lines 140/179/279. `_expand` is a plain def called from two async endpoints, so either make it async and await the `completed_cells` call off-thread, or hoist that call into the callers. `storage.init_db()` at line 85 is startup-only and can stay.

confirmed.title: save_image's cleanup handler deletes the finished image even when the row has already committed
confirmed.description: The guard is `except BaseException: _unlink(partial); raise`, but the try block spans two very different things: the INSERT and the rename. `_session()` commits on leaving `with conn:`, so by the time `partial.replace(path)` runs the row is durable. If the rename then raises, the handler deletes the only copy of the image while the row it belongs to stays in the database. The comment reasons only about 'a failed INSERT' - it has no way to tell the two cases apart.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced by making `Path.replace` raise PermissionError(32) - the failure the file's own comment at line 158 cites as motivating: save_image raises, rows committed 1, the row names a filename, nothing is on disk, and clear_history then reports records 1, files_on_disk 0, orphan_files 0. On Windows 11 - the documented native platform - `os.replace` on a source file another process holds open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE fails with ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION (32) or ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5), and a just-closed 5-15 MB PNG is precisely what Defender real-time scanning, a search indexer or a OneDrive/Dropbox watcher opens. One blip costs the image permanently (24 s of GPU on a 2 MP Turbo render) and leaves a phantom gallery row whose file 404s forever; the exception also propagates into `jobs._generate`, which has no per-image guard, so the job goes to error and the rest of the grid never runs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only tidy up when the row did not commit: set a `committed = True` flag after the with block and make the handler `if not committed: _unlink(partial)`. Better still, retry the rename a few times with a short backoff before giving up - the AV or indexer handle is held for milliseconds. Pair with a `.part` sweeper so the survivor does not become permanent litter.

confirmed.title: The per-cell SSE status event ships the whole accumulated images array, making a grid's stream quadratic in its cell count
confirmed.description: `_generate` emits one status event per cell as `{"type": "status", **job.snapshot()}`, and `Job.snapshot()` includes `"images": self.images` - every ImageRecord the job has produced so far. Cell N therefore re-transmits N-1 records already delivered as their own `image` events, and `main.job_stream` json.dumps-es each of those on the event loop, once per attached subscriber. The client does not need them: status handling is `if (data.images) data.images.forEach(show)` and `show()` discards anything whose id it has seen. The backlog only matters on the attach snapshot and on `done`, both of which would keep it. `GET /api/jobs` already strips images from the snapshot with the comment 'a long sweep accumulates hundreds of records', so the omission here is inconsistent rather than deliberate. This is the previous review's unverified `jobs.py:199` entry, still unfixed - the line moved to 258 when runs became cells.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Measured over a real stream with the FakeBackend, a 64-cell grid (1 step per cell, 200-character prompt): status 64 events / 1,209,741 bytes; image 64 events / 41,939 bytes; progress 63 events / 7,615 bytes. The status events are 29x the payload that carries new information and grow as N^2. A separate end-to-end measurement of a 1000-cell grid gave 258 MiB of status events against 586 KiB of image events - 450x amplification - and at the shipped ceiling of 1024 cells with prompts near the 4000-character cap it reaches multiple GB, all produced by json.dumps on the event loop and duplicated per attached tab. Secondary: job.images is retained for the life of the job and _jobs keeps up to 200 jobs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give `snapshot()` an `images: bool = True` switch and use `job.snapshot(images=False)` for the per-cell event only; `events()`'s opening snapshot and `_finish`'s done must keep the list, since a reattaching client depends on it. The client's `if (data.images)` guard already tolerates the key being absent, and main.py:302 can then use the same switch instead of filtering the key out by hand. Hand out `list(self.images)` wherever images stay in a frame - the snapshot currently shares the live list, so what json.dumps serialises is not the list as of emit time.

confirmed.title: The recorded negative prompt is not the one that ran, and it silently defeats --resume
confirmed.description: The backend drops the negative prompt when it cannot apply (`if supported and request.negative_prompt and request.guidance_scale > threshold`), but nothing tells storage. `jobs._generate` and `generate.py` both hand `save_image` the untouched request, and `save_image` writes `request.negative_prompt` unconditionally into the DB row, into the `krea` JSON chunk and into the PNG's A1111 parameters block. This makes CLAUDE.md lines 77-79 false: 'Dropping the negative prompt below the threshold ... only keeps the recorded settings honest about what ran' - the drop is invisible to the record, so the guard now delivers nothing. The two configurations where it bites are both profile defaults: Krea 2 Turbo (threshold 0.0, profile guidance 0.0, so 0.0 > 0.0 is False) and FLUX.2 klein (supported is False; the code even logs 'this pipeline takes no negative prompt; ignoring it'). All three clients feed it - `collect()` reads a disabled textarea's value, generate.py prints '[ignored: CFG is at or below 0]' and then passes the same string to save_image, and /docs has no filter at all. The same shape hits mu: on a pipeline with no `sigmas` parameter and a non-shifting scheduler, mu is blanked and the kwarg popped, yet request.mu is still written to the row.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Turbo at profile defaults. Night 1: POST /api/grid with negative_prompt 'blurry, low quality', steps_axis '6,8', seeds 8, seed 100 - 16 cells. The pipeline never sees the negative prompt; all 16 rows record it. The run dies at cell 9. Next morning the user notices the field is greyed at CFG 0, clears it, ticks Resume and re-submits with the same seed. Every cell_key now carries None where every row carries 'blurry, low quality', so prune_done matches nothing: the preview says 0 already done and the job re-renders all 16 cells, 8 of them pixel-identical duplicates at full GPU cost. Separately, any A1111-compatible tool reading one of these PNGs applies a negative prompt the image was never generated with. The mu variant is worse still, because mu is part of the resume key: an image made with no shift at all is recorded as mu=1.15, so `mu:none` never finds it and prune_done treats a mu=1.15 cell as already rendered.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the two sides agree on one normalisation. Smallest self-consistent version: `collect()` sends `negative_prompt: els.negative.disabled ? null : (...)`, and generate.py reuses the branch that already decides its note, passing None when it resolves to ignored. The complete version has the backend report what it applied - it already computes `supported` and `threshold` - e.g. `applies_negative_prompt(request) -> bool`, with jobs._generate and generate.py saving `req.model_copy(update=...)` when it answers False; `main._expand` must normalise cell keys the same way before prune_done, falling back to the profile's guess when no pipeline is loaded. Correct CLAUDE.md lines 77-79 in the same change, and while in save_image, add mu to the A1111 parameters block for the same 'other tools can read the params back' reason.

confirmed.title: Quantization is not in the record or the resume key, so an fp8 cell satisfies a resume running at int8 or nunchaku
confirmed.description: `completed_cells` scopes its lookup to width, height and model_id, and the key it returns is (prompt, negative, steps, CFG, mu, seed). Quantization and offload are not in it - and cannot be, because nothing persists them: the images schema has no such column, the PNG krea chunk carries model and job but not the quantizer, and ImageRecord carries model_id only. `quantization` appears exactly once in the whole persistence surface, as ModelStatus.quantization, which is live status rather than history. But quantization is part of the reproduction set - config.py says so itself: fp8 is '~12GB', int8 'smaller still, slightly softer output', nunchaku SVDQuant W4A4. Same seed, same everything else, different quantizer, different pixels. CLAUDE.md's resume bullet names the key without mentioning quantization, so this is a gap in the documented design rather than a documented decision.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `python -m backend.generate "a lighthouse in fog" --seed 42 --grid-cfg 0-4x1 --grid-seeds 4 --quant fp8` queues 20 cells and is killed after 9. The next run is `--resume --quant int8` - or a bare `python -m backend.main` that takes the fp8 default on a bare Enter after an int8 night, which CLAUDE.md documents as the menu's behaviour. It prints 'resume : 9 cell(s) already rendered, skipping' and renders the remaining 11 under a different quantizer. The contact sheet whose entire purpose is comparing CFG across a fixed seed then has 9 cells from one numerical pipeline and 11 from another, with no column, badge, filter or PNG field distinguishing them. Independently, Reuse on any card silently produces a different image whenever the server is on a different quantizer than the run that made it, and there is no way to find out which that was.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Persist it and key on it: add `quantization TEXT` (and optionally `offload TEXT`) to _SCHEMA and _migrate - the job_id migration is the precedent - pass settings.quantization into save_image beside model_id, put it in the krea chunk and on ImageRecord, extend completed_cells's WHERE to `AND (quantization IS NULL OR quantization = ?)` so an existing gallery keeps resuming, and add `quant:` to _FILTERS so a mixed gallery can be separated after the fact. Update the CLAUDE.md resume bullet to name quantization as part of the key. Offload is likely bit-identical (same kernels, same dtypes, different residency), so recording it is documentation rather than a key.

confirmed.title: Reuse restores a record's checkpoint-specific settings onto whatever checkpoint is loaded, with no warning
confirmed.description: `reuse(rec)` restores prompt, negative prompt, size, steps, CFG, mu and seed, and never looks at `rec.model_id`. It cannot: `refreshStatus` reads `s.model_id` only to build the status-bar text; unlike `cfgThreshold` and `negativeSupported`, which are kept in module state precisely so the rest of the page can consult them, the loaded checkpoint is never stored. The gallery is a single index shared by every checkpoint and the launch menu makes switching a start-up question, so a gallery routinely holds Turbo rows (8 / 0.0 / 1.15) alongside FLUX rows (28 / 3.5 / null), and Reuse moves one onto the other silently. The code already knows this is wrong: `renderLightbox` carries the comment 'The checkpoint is part of the reproduction set as much as the seed is' and prints the model id for exactly that reason. It also latches - `reuse()` calls `ownControls()`, which sets defaultsApplied, so the wrong values survive every subsequent /api/status poll for the session.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Server started on the default checkpoint, FLUX.1 Krea [dev]; the gallery still holds last week's Turbo images. The user clicks Reuse on one and presses Generate. The request is steps=8, guidance_scale=0.0, mu=1.15 against FLUX: 8 steps is well under the range the profile's own hint calls degraded, guidance 0.0 replaces FLUX's distilled 3.5 conditioning value, and mu=1.15 goes through _forced_mu to override calculate_shift, which at 2048x2048 derives roughly 3.2 - which CLAUDE.md says degrades output. The result is a visibly broken image recorded under FLUX with settings that reproduce nothing, and the panel stays on those numbers for the rest of the session.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the loaded checkpoint in module state next to the other two server-followed values (`currentModel = s.model_id` in refreshStatus) and flag the mismatch in `reuse()` - a non-blocking hint line under the seed field is better than showError if it should not look like a failure. The stronger option, restoring prompt/size/seed but leaving steps/CFG/mu on the current profile when the checkpoints differ, is defensible but changes what Reuse means; warn first.

confirmed.title: The negative-prompt gate is computed from the panel's single CFG, which is neither what a grid runs nor what gets recorded
confirmed.description: `syncCfg()` disables the textarea whenever `+els.cfg.value <= cfgThreshold`, with two consequences in opposite directions. First, a grid's CFG axis decides guidance per cell - `gridPayload()` spreads `collect()` and adds cfg_axis, and `grid.expand` builds each cell with its own guidance_scale while inheriting negative_prompt from the base request - but the gate reads only the panel's single value. On Turbo the profile default is CFG 0 with threshold 0, so the field is disabled the moment /api/status lands, while the grid CFG placeholder in index.html is literally `0,0.5,1`. Second, `collect()` reads `els.negative.value` with no reference to that gate at all, so a disabled, greyed-out field still ships its contents. This is the previous review's unverified `app.js:187` entry, still unfixed, and FLUX.2 klein makes it permanent: negative_prompt_supported false greys the field for the whole session, yet every image of that session records whatever text is sitting in it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Krea 2 Turbo, panel CFG 0, grid CFG axis 0,0.5,1: the textarea is disabled, so the two guided cells of every comparison run against no negative prompt and there is no way from the UI to give them one - which is precisely the comparison a CFG sweep is for, and the note under the field reads '(needs CFG > 0 - ~2x slower)' while describing a run that crosses that threshold. Reading such a sweep in the morning, the user attributes the jump between the CFG 1 and CFG 2 columns to guidance strength; half of it is the negative prompt switching on, and neither the sheet's column headers nor the lightbox meta line nor the PNG metadata says so.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Gate on the highest CFG the submission can reach, not on the panel value: when the grid section is open and the CFG axis is non-empty, take the max of the resolved axis values (the preview response already carries them as `p.values.guidance_scale`). And make `collect()` honour the gate it draws: `negative_prompt: els.negative.disabled ? null : (...)`. The server-side half - recording a negative prompt the backend dropped - needs the same treatment in save_image; see the diffusers_backend.py:403 entry.

confirmed.title: Contact sheet: an axis promoted to Columns or Rows stays in sheetAxes.pins, blanking every cell outside the pinned value
confirmed.description: `chooseAxes` pins every varying axis past the second. The Columns picker's callback swaps rows and cols when the chosen key is already on the other side, but it never removes the chosen key from `sheetAxes.pins`; the Rows callback is identical. `axisOptions` offers every varying axis, pinned ones included, so choosing one is a normal action. `renderSheet` then keeps the stale pin - the signature check only re-derives the layout when the per-axis value counts change, and picking a different axis changes none of them - so the pin loop still renders a picker for it and `matches()` still demands `axisValue(axis, rec) === pinned` on the axis that is now the column. `matches()` applies the pin filter before the row and column comparisons, so only one column of that axis can ever be populated.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A grid of 3 prompts x 2 steps x 2 CFG = 12 images, opened with the Sheet button. The default layout is cols=Prompt, rows=Steps, pinned CFG=first value - 6 cells filled. Set the Columns dropdown to CFG. The result is a 2-column sheet whose second CFG column is entirely `.sheet-cell.empty`, a CFG pin dropdown still on screen next to a Columns dropdown that also says CFG, and a note reading '2 of 12 loaded - pinned to cfg 0'. The Prompt axis, freed by the swap, is now neither an axis nor a pin, so the per-cell find silently shows one arbitrary prompt per cell with nothing saying which. Toggling Sheet off and on does not clear it, because sheetAxes is module state the signature never invalidates.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Maintain the invariant that every varying axis is exactly one of columns, rows or a pin. Replace both handlers with one helper that swaps the other side on collision, deletes the promoted axis from pins, and re-pins whatever it displaced; or reconcile the whole pin set on every render after the signature block. Also drop a pin whose value is no longer in `values[key]` - indexOf already returns -1 there, leaving a select that shows one value while filtering on another.

confirmed.title: Contact-sheet pins survive a change of run, because the layout signature is axis cardinalities only
confirmed.description: `renderSheet` re-derives the layout only when the shape changes: the signature is `SHEET_AXES.map((a) => values[a.key].length).join('/')`. That is five counts, not the values behind them, while `sheetAxes.pins` holds actual values compared by identity in `matches()`. Switching the gallery search from one run to another of the same shape - job:A to job:B, two runs of the same grid at different seeds - leaves the signature unchanged, keeps run A's pins.seed, and no record of run B matches it. This is a different mechanism from the promoted-axis entry above: that one is triggered by the axis pickers, this one by the record set changing underneath a kept layout.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Click Sheet on an image from last night's run, then on an image from tonight's re-run of the same grid (or on the second half of a resumed night). The sheet is entirely blank with the note '0 of 24 loaded - pinned to seed 42' while the Seed dropdown shows 100 - because `picker()` marks selected by string comparison and indexOf(pinned) is -1, so the browser displays the first option while the filter is on the invisible one. Choosing the displayed value fires no change event, so the obvious fix does nothing, and setSheet(false)/setSheet(true) does not reset sheetAxes either. Only a reload, or a differently-shaped result set, clears it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Invalidate on the values rather than the counts (join each axis's key with its value list), or keep the cheap signature and clamp each pin after the check to a value that is actually present. Also reset `sheetAxes` in `setSheet(false)` so toggling the view is a real escape hatch.

confirmed.title: Resume marks a whole batch cell done when only its first image committed
confirmed.description: `grid.cell_key()` identifies a cell by `cell.seed` - the base seed. `storage.completed_cells()` builds its key set from one row per image, and `jobs._generate` writes each image of a batch under `wrap_seed(seed + offset)`. With num_images == 1 the two coincide; with num_images > 1 they do not, so only image 0's row can ever match a cell key and a single committed row declares the whole cell rendered. Nothing counts rows per cell: GridPreview.skipped counts cells and `images = len(cells) * num_images` assumes every surviving cell is untouched and every pruned cell complete.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified against the shipped code with no GPU: a request with seed 1000 and num_images 4, expanded over steps '8,10' and seeds 2, gives cells at (8,1000), (10,1000), (8,1004), (10,1004); feeding prune_done a done set containing only cell_key(cells[0]) - what storage returns when seed 1000 alone committed - drops cell (8,1000) entirely, though it should have produced seeds 1000-1003. Operationally: a grid with Batch 4 left running overnight stops between saves at 03:00 (power cut, disk full, a transient 'database is locked' from a backup tool or a concurrent clear.py VACUUM). In the morning the user ticks Resume and re-submits the identical grid as README instructs; the cell is silently skipped and images 1-3 of it are never rendered. The contact sheet still shows a picture in that square, so the hole is invisible there too.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the completeness test cover the whole batch: add `cell_keys(cell, num_images)` returning one key per per-image seed and have `prune_done(cells, done, num_images)` keep a cell unless every key is present. main._expand passes request.num_images, generate.main passes args.batch; completed_cells needs no change, since it already returns one key per image. Add a test that a done set holding only the base seed of a 4-image cell does not prune that cell.

confirmed.title: A resumed night is split across two job ids, and the contact sheet can only ever show one half
confirmed.description: Resume is documented as the way a dead night is continued: a new job renders the cells the gallery is short. `jobs.submit_cells` mints a fresh uuid4 hex per submission and save_image stamps every image with it, so after one resume the grid's images carry two different job_ids. Everything built to read a run back is keyed on exactly one of them: the card's sheet button hard-codes `els.search.value = 'job:' + rec.job_id`, and the search grammar cannot express the union - `list_images` AND-joins every predicate, so two job: terms are unsatisfiable and a comma list becomes one LIKE that matches nothing (confirmed against the shipped parser). The settings-based workaround is worse than nothing: a search spanning both halves also drags in every earlier image at those settings, and renderSheet's find takes the first match in newest-first order, so duplicate settings silently put the wrong image in the square.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 1024-cell grid dies at cell 700. In the morning the user resumes as documented and the remaining 324 land under a second job id. Clicking the sheet button on any image now yields a sheet of at most 700 or at most 324 cells, with every square from the other half rendered empty and the note reading '700 of 700 loaded'. The complete matrix - the single artefact the whole grid feature exists to produce - cannot be displayed at all, and a night interrupted three times fragments into four unjoinable sheets, with nothing in the UI hinting at why.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give a grid a stable identity independent of the job that ran it: a `run_id` column derived on the server from the run's own definition (a hash of model_id, size, base seed, sorted resolved axes and distinct prompts), computed in main._expand and passed through submit_cells into save_image, so a resume of the same grid recomputes the same id. Point the sheet button at `run:<id>`, add run to storage._FILTERS, and fall back to job: for older rows. Smaller stopgap that fixes only the reading half: let _filter_clause OR a comma-separated list for the string filters, and have startJob remember the id it just queued.

confirmed.title: A prompt full of {placeholders} with an empty variables box escapes the grid's own mismatch guard
confirmed.description: `prompt_assignments()` returns `[{}]` before it computes `used = _placeholders(request)`, so the two mismatch checks that follow - nothing in the prompt says {name}, and {name} has no values - never run when the variables block is empty. `substitute(text, {})` then returns the prompt unchanged, so `{size} dog sitting on {ground}` is encoded verbatim. Three documents assert this cannot happen: CLAUDE.md ('a placeholder with no variable renders the literal {ground} into every image of the run'), README ('Both are caught when you submit, not at 3am'), and tests/test_grid.py, whose five parametrised mismatch cases all supply at least one variable - so the hole is exactly the case the suite does not reach. `_placeholders` reads the negative prompt too, so a {name} there alone has the same hole.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified at HEAD: expanding a request whose prompt is `{size} dog sitting on {ground}` with an empty variables block, steps '6,8' and seeds 2 yields 4 cells, every one carrying the literal braces, while the same request with `size = big | small` is correctly refused with 'prompt: {ground} has no values'. The browser gives no other signal: promptLines() returns [] when fewer than 2 prompts resolve, so the preview prints only the image count and never shows the prompt it resolved to. The easiest mistake in the feature - writing the placeholders and forgetting to fill the variables box, or clearing it while keeping the prompt - therefore produces a full-length overnight run in which every image was conditioned on literal braces: a 480-cell night is four hours of GPU time and 480 useless PNGs, all committed, all counted as done by --resume, and indistinguishable on the contact sheet.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Move the placeholder check above the early return: compute `used = _placeholders(request)` first and, when there are no variables, raise if used is non-empty. That keeps 'a grid with no axes set is exactly the image Generate would have made' for a prompt with no placeholders, which is what index.html's 'Blank runs the prompt exactly as written' is about. Add the missing parametrised case to tests/test_grid.py. If a literal {WORD} must stay possible, add an escape rather than keeping the silent path.

confirmed.title: One cell's exception abandons every remaining cell of a grid; only Cancelled is handled per-cell
confirmed.description: `_generate` catches exactly one exception inside its cell loop - `except Cancelled` - and `storage.save_image` is not inside any try at all. Every other exception escapes the loop, propagates out of run_in_executor, and is caught in `_run`, which sets status error and emits the terminal event; the remaining cells are silently discarded, the list simply never iterated further. This is the opposite of what the cancellation path does two lines above and of what CLAUDE.md promises for it. An exception is treated as fatal even for failures that are transient and cell-local: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError when another process briefly takes VRAM, or sqlite3.OperationalError from a concurrent clear.py. generate.py has the identical shape - except Exception outside the loop, return 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 512-cell overnight grid at 2 MP, six hours in, 400 cells rendered. At 02:00 something else on the desktop takes 2 GB of VRAM and cell 401 raises OutOfMemoryError at step 3 of 8. The job goes to error and the other 111 cells are dropped. In the morning the user has a red status and an incomplete matrix, and recovery requires a new grid with resume and the run's original base seed - which, if the grid was submitted with the seed box empty, exists nowhere the UI will show. Continuing to the next cell would have cost one image.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make a cell failure a cell-level event with a consecutive-failure cap so a genuinely dead pipeline still stops quickly: catch Exception (after Cancelled, which subclasses it), record job.error, emit a per-cell error event, continue, and re-raise after 3 consecutive failures; reset the counter on success and add a total cap so a marginal failure hitting one cell in three does not limp all night. Derive the terminal status in `_run` from the failure count rather than leaving line 217's cancelled/done to decide, and note that a new SSE event type is invisible until web/app.js's closed if/else over progress|image|status|done gains a branch - putting failures in snapshot() is the smaller change. Mirror it in generate.py's loop.

confirmed.title: short_error truncates the tail of a CUDA OOM - the only actionable sentence - and the untruncated text exists nowhere at the shipped log level
confirmed.description: `short_error` joins the non-'Request ID' lines of str(exc) and, past 320 characters, keeps the head and drops the tail. PyTorch builds its OOM message with the diagnosis first and the remedy last; the template strings in this checkout's own c10_cuda.dll end with 'If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation.' Filled in with plausible numbers and without the optional non-PyTorch-memory clause that is 508 characters, and the prefix alone reaches 230, so the cut at 319 lands inside the environment variable name. The full text is then unrecoverable: _run logs it as `log.debug("job traceback", exc_info=True)` and ensure_loaded likewise, while `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` is hard-coded with no environment override anywhere in the repo. The same DEBUG-only pattern hides 'scheduler takes no mu; ignoring mu=...' and the silent dropping of pipeline kwargs.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A 4 MP generation OOMs. The user sees a one-line red banner ending mid-token in PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandabl..., and there is nothing in the terminal but the same truncated line. The one setting that would fix their problem is the part that was cut; to see it they have to edit main.py and restart.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Two independent changes: log the untruncated message where it can be read (`log.error("job %s failed: %s", job.id, exc)`, or promote the two exc_info=True calls to log.exception, and/or read the level from KREA_LOG_LEVEL); and when short_error must cut, cut from the middle - keep two thirds of the head and the last third - so the closing sentence survives.

confirmed.title: No downscaled derivative exists: 5 MB 2048-square PNGs are decoded to fill 160 px cards and 96 px sheet cells
confirmed.description: Every thumbnail in the app points at the original file. `card()` sets `img.src = rec.url` into a `.card` in a `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr))` grid; `renderSheet` does the same into `.sheet-cell` at `minmax(96px, 1fr)`. `rec.url` is `/outputs/{filename}`, mounted as-is by StaticFiles, and `save_image` writes exactly one artefact. Grepping for a derivative returns only three comments that assert 'the thumbnails load lazily' - lazy they are; thumbnails they are not. Measured with Pillow at the code's own compress_level=4: a representative 2048x2048 output is 5.08 MB on disk and 16.8 MB decoded; 1024x1024 is 1.35 MB / 4.2 MB. The backend is not the bottleneck - against a 20,000-row synthetic gallery, GET /api/gallery?limit=48 measured 4.4 ms / 18 KiB and limit=1024 measured 14.2 ms / 383 KiB - the bytes are all image.
confirmed.failure_scenario: At the 4 MP tier a default gallery viewport of ~24 cards decodes ~400 MB of bitmap to paint 24 160-px squares. Nine clicks of 'Load more' to reach a 500-image page transfers ~2.5 GB from /outputs, and because Chrome discards decoded data for far-offscreen images, every scroll back re-decodes 5 MB PNGs at 40-80 ms each - so the gallery janks exactly when you are hunting through a night's output for the good frames. The contact sheet is worse per pixel: a full-res 2048-square PNG per 96 px cell.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Write a sidecar derivative in save_image (a ~384 px JPEG or WEBP, ~10 ms against the PNG's ~197 ms), add thumb_url to ImageRecord derived in _row_to_record, and use `rec.thumb_url ?? rec.url` in card() and the sheet cell while the lightbox and the viewer keep the full image (the viewer's .multi tier is larger than 384 px, so a thumb there would blur the image the user just made). Falling back to rec.url when the sidecar is absent backfills the existing gallery for free. Two places must learn the new suffix or they will leak and mis-report: clear_history's delete and orphan passes and summarise() glob *.png, and delete_image unlinks only record.filename - writing the thumb into a subdirectory keeps the orphan sweep safe but means nothing ever reclaims it, so add an explicit unlink and a thumbs pass. Keep the .part-then-rename discipline for the thumb, and write it after the rename so a failed INSERT leaves no thumb for a row that never existed.

confirmed.title: A cleared CFG box silently generates at guidance 0; the UI never uses the schema's 'not given' contract
confirmed.description: `collect()` coerces every numeric control with unary plus, and for an emptied number input - cleared to retype, or holding text the browser rejects - value is '' and +'' === 0. steps, num_images, runs, width and height are then rejected by the schema's ge= bounds and surface as a readable 422 (readableDetail landed since the last review), but guidance_scale has ge=0.0, so 0 is a valid value and the run proceeds unguided. Meanwhile schemas.py was rebuilt precisely so an omitted steps/guidance_scale means 'the loaded checkpoint's profile', with mu distinguishing absent from explicit null via model_fields_set - and the UI, the client that contract was written for, never exercises it: only mu and seed map empty to a meaningful value. This is the previous review's unverified `app.js:194` entry, still open in its sharpest half.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On the default checkpoint (FLUX.1 Krea dev, profile CFG 3.5) the user selects the CFG box, presses Backspace to clear it, and hits Ctrl+Enter - which generates from anywhere, including from inside a field - before typing the new number. The run goes out at guidance_scale 0: a materially different image, with the negative prompt silently dropped in the same gesture because syncCfg greys the field at or below the threshold. The record stores 0.0, so nothing downstream ever looks inconsistent and Reuse reproduces the wrong-but-consistent settings. gridPayload() spreads collect(), so an overnight grid inherits it and every cell runs at 0.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make an empty control mean 'not given' and let the server's profile validator fill it - JSON.stringify drops undefined, so nothing else changes: `const num = (el) => (el.value.trim() === '' ? undefined : +el.value);` for steps and guidance_scale at minimum. Leave width/height coerced (the presets always populate them, and a silent 1024 would be worse than the 422 they get today). If the current 422s on a cleared Steps/Batch/Runs are preferred to a silent profile default, restrict the change to guidance_scale alone, or refuse to submit while any numeric box is empty.

confirmed.title: The unsupported-kwarg filter silently drops callback_on_step_end and generator, the two arguments the backend contract is built on
confirmed.description: `generate()` assembles kwargs and then removes anything the loaded pipeline does not accept, at log.debug. The loop makes no distinction between an optional argument (guidance_scale, sigmas, num_images_per_prompt) and the two that carry documented guarantees. `callback_on_step_end` is the only place the pipeline hands control back, so it is both the progress source and, per backends/base.py, the mandatory cancellation point. `generator` is the per-image seed list that CLAUDE.md's 'one generator per image, seeded seed + i' rule depends on and that save_image records next to each PNG. Both are dropped at DEBUG, invisible at the shipped log_level=INFO, so nothing reports that the guarantee is gone. The module docstring and the start-up menu's free-text option both actively invite pointing KREA_MODEL_ID at an arbitrary diffusers text-to-image repo, and diffusers still ships text-to-image pipelines exposing the old callback/callback_steps pair.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Point KREA_MODEL_ID at a repo whose pipeline predates callback_on_step_end. The load succeeds, /api/status says ready, and generation works - but the progress bar sits at 0/N for the whole run, Job.step never advances, and POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel sets a flag on a job that will never look at it: Cancel does nothing, the CLI's Ctrl-C never lands, and jobs.shutdown() waits out the entire remaining sweep. If generator is the one missing, every image is drawn from unseeded noise while the gallery row, the filename and the PNG metadata all record a seed that reproduces nothing. In both cases the only trace is a DEBUG line nobody is logging.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Split the loop: keep the silent drop for optional arguments and fail loudly for the contract-critical ones. Better still, check `self._call_params` at the end of load() and refuse there, so the failure arrives before the first image rather than per call. At minimum promote the drop log from debug to warning.

confirmed.title: Touching Steps, CFG, Mu or Seed before the first /api/status lands freezes all three sampling controls at the generic fallback profile
confirmed.description: `applyDefaults` is the only thing that ever puts the checkpoint's profile into the panel, and it is all-or-nothing behind one flag: `if (defaultsApplied || !d || d.steps === undefined) return;`. `ownControls()` sets that flag and is wired to four inputs - Steps, Mu, CFG and Seed. index.html ships the _FALLBACK profile's numbers (28 / 3.5 / blank), not the loaded checkpoint's. The window is not small: /api/status computes its whole response through `await asyncio.to_thread(backend.describe)`, and describe() is the first place in the server process that imports torch - nothing at import time does, since the backend module's torch imports are all function-local. Measured here with a warm file cache, `import torch` is 1.28 s; cold on Windows with a CUDA init behind it, several seconds. `applyHints` is not gated by the flag, so the tooltip updates to the real checkpoint's wording while the boxes keep the fallback numbers - the only visible tell.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Server started on krea/Krea-2-Turbo; the page loads; within the first 1.5-5 s the user clicks into Seed and pastes a number. defaultsApplied is now true, /api/status lands and is ignored, and the panel stays at 28 steps / CFG 3.5 instead of Turbo's 8 / 0.0. Generate then runs Turbo at 3.5x the denoising work and, because 3.5 is above Turbo's 0.0 threshold, adds an uncond pass per step - roughly 7x the intended time per image, over-guided, with the tooltip beside the box reading 'Turbo is trained for 0'. The row records 28/3.5 faithfully, so Reuse reproduces it. Same shape on klein (28 instead of 4) and klein-base (28/3.5 instead of 50/4.0); invisible on FLUX.1 only because its profile equals the fallback. Secondary: Mu stays blank, so Turbo images record mu NULL where a seeded panel records 1.15 - the same schedule filed under two keys, which splits mu:none from mu:1.15 and makes the two sets non-interchangeable for resume.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make ownership per-control instead of global - track steps/cfg/mu separately, set only the field whose oninput fired, and have applyDefaults fill in each control the user has not touched. Drop ownControls() from els.seed.oninput entirely: the seed is not a sampling value and has no business freezing the profile. Independently, stop making the first status call pay for `import torch` - warm it once from lifespan, or split a cheap /api/status answered from settings and _load_state from the VRAM numbers the UI only needs for a badge.

confirmed.title: The Resume checkbox fires no preview, so the grid panel never shows the skipped count the server computes for it
confirmed.description: The preview is re-run only by the elements listed at app.js:1028-1032 plus the details toggle. `els.gridResume` is read exactly once, in gridPayload(); it has no input or change handler. So the whole resume half of /api/grid/preview is unreachable from the gesture it exists for: the server computes `skipped` and the client already knows how to render it, but ticking the box changes nothing on screen. `els.negative` is missing from the same list, so editing a {name} placeholder that lives in the negative prompt - which grid._placeholders validates - also leaves a stale preview behind.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The exact flow this feature was built for: a 480-cell grid died overnight at cell 300. In the morning the user re-enters the grid, ticks Resume, and reads '480 images - 4 steps x 3 CFG x 2 mu x 20 seeds - about 4h 10m' - the un-pruned numbers, with no '300 already done' and a duration off by 60%. They then click Run grid and get either a job that is actually 180 cells or a bare 409 'every cell is already rendered', with no warning that the preview they approved was for a different run. A user who edits any other field afterwards does see it, which makes the behaviour look intermittent rather than broken.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add the missing listeners: a change handler on els.gridResume calling previewGrid immediately (it is one click) and an input handler on els.negative calling schedulePreview. Note the knock-on: once Resume can be ticked, every subsequent keystroke sends resume: true and makes the preview run storage.completed_cells - synchronous SQLite on the event loop, filed separately. Land this alongside moving that call to asyncio.to_thread, or debounce the resume-carrying preview harder.

confirmed.title: The menu's checkpoint default silently discards a KREA_MODEL_ID the catalogue does not know
confirmed.description: `_prompt` resolves the environment's checkpoint through `_match`, which only recognises the seven catalogue repos and their lite re-uploads. Any other id returns (None, None), default stays 0, and the marker lands on entry 1, FLUX.1 Krea [dev]. Every other prompt in the menu handles this case - `_index` falls back only after checking membership, and the quant/offload/format lists always contain their fallback - but the checkpoint list has no 'keep what you have' row, only a free-text option that must be typed. The header says 'Enter keeps the marked default' and CLAUDE.md asserts 'the environment's values are the marked defaults'; both are false for any id outside the catalogue, including ids the menu itself produces, since _pick's free-text branch exists precisely to accept repos the catalogue does not list and configure() then writes that id into KREA_MODEL_ID.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by running the menu directly: KREA_MODEL_ID=nobody/whatever plus three bare Enters returns model_id='black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev' with entry 1 marked. Operationally that is a round-trip failure through the menu's own free-text option: start bare, choose 'another repo id', type a repo; restart bare, press Enter three times as the header instructs, and the server starts FLUX instead - a click-through-gated ~32 GB download on a cold cache, minutes of load, and every image of that session recorded under the wrong model_id, so --resume and completed_cells for the intended checkpoint match nothing. Same for a local checkpoint directory or any Hub repo the catalogue has not been taught.
confirmed.suggested_fix: List the unrecognised current id as a real entry so Enter can keep it: after the catalogue loop, if KREA_MODEL_ID is set and unmatched, append it to entries, add it to repos so `repos.get(answer, answer)` stays correct, and point default at it. Add a test alongside test_a_lite_repo_in_the_environment_marks_its_family_and_format: env KREA_MODEL_ID=nobody/whatever, bare Enters, assert the id survives.

confirmed.title: env.sh defaults KREA_MODEL_ID to a pre-quantized Nunchaku repo unconditionally, so overriding only KREA_QUANT pairs torchao with an already-quantized checkpoint
confirmed.description: wsl/env.sh guards its two coupled settings independently: line 21 defaults KREA_QUANT to nunchaku, line 22 defaults KREA_MODEL_ID to a lite-infer NVFP4 repo whatever line 21 resolved to. README.md:131 says 'Any other KREA_QUANT value works from WSL too; set it before sourcing env.sh' - do exactly that and you get quantization=fp8 paired with a Nunchaku-quantized checkpoint. Everywhere else quant decides the repo family: launch._prompt asks quantization first for that reason and _match() maps a lite repo back to its official sibling, so the menu path recovers - but the menu is skipped by any argument, and `bash wsl/serve.sh --defaults` is documented. The backend has no guard in this direction: _nunchaku_preflight runs only when quantization is nunchaku, so fp8 falls straight through and builds a PipelineQuantizationConfig for a repo whose text_encoder/config.json already carries a BitsAndBytesConfig. The same unconditional default hard-codes nvfp4 in the repo name even though wsl/setup.sh has already computed the card's compute capability and printed 'pre-Blackwell: use the int4 repos'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: From a WSL shell: `export KREA_QUANT=fp8 && source wsl/env.sh && bash wsl/serve.sh --defaults`, then one generate request. The server downloads ~9 GB of NVFP4 transformer plus NF4 text-encoder weights over several minutes, then dies with 'ValueError: The model is quantized with BitsAndBytesConfig but you are passing a TorchAoConfig config.' from deep inside transformers (verified in the installed transformers 5.16.1). _nunchaku_preflight exists specifically to refuse before the download for the mirror-image mistake; the reverse pairing gets no such protection. `python -m backend.generate` in the same shell fails identically, with no menu to recover through.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Condition line 22 on the mode, so a non-nunchaku quant falls through to config.py's own default, and interpolate the format rather than hard-coding nvfp4. Add the symmetric preflight in _quantization_config(): when quantization is fp8 or int8, read transformer/config.json through the existing _hub_file() (one small file, no snapshot) and raise if it already names a quant_method. Reword README.md:131 to say that overriding KREA_QUANT means also naming a matching KREA_MODEL_ID.

confirmed.title: grid.py varies the negative prompt through the same {name} placeholders, but SHEET_AXES has no negative-prompt axis, so such a run collapses to a single cell
confirmed.description: `grid._placeholders` collects placeholders from the prompt and the negative prompt, and `grid.expand` substitutes into both, so a variable that appears only in the negative prompt is a legal, fully supported axis. SHEET_AXES enumerates what the sheet can lay out - prompt, steps, cfg, mu, seed - and the negative prompt is not there, even though ImageRecord.negative_prompt carries it to the client. `grid.axis_values` also reports values['prompt'] as the substituted prompt list, so a negative-only variable yields duplicate prompt strings and the preview prints the same prompt twice as if it were two.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified by running the expansion: prompt 'a dog', negative prompt '{style}', variables `style = blurry | grainy` yields two cells with identical prompt/steps/CFG/mu/seed, negative prompts blurry and grainy, two distinct cell_keys, and describe() saying '2 prompts x 1 steps x 1 CFG x 1 mu x 1 seed'. On the sheet, sheetValues finds every one of the five axes has exactly one distinct value, so chooseAxes returns no axes at all and the whole run renders as one cell; axisOptions only offers axes with more than one value, so the pickers contain nothing but em-dashes and the user cannot recover the layout by hand. The realistic version - negative {style} with four values crossed with 4 seeds, 16 images - renders one image with the note '1 of 16 loaded'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add the axis: `{ key: 'negative', label: 'Negative', of: (r) => r.negative_prompt || null }` to SHEET_AXES - valueText already renders null as `none` - with the same promptLabels/clip treatment a long value will want. Separately, make grid.axis_values report the negative prompt where it varies (or dedupe values['prompt']) so the preview's '2 prompts' and its duplicated bullet lines stop lying, and mention negative-prompt placeholders in the index.html tooltip and README, which currently say only 'Put {name} placeholders in the prompt'.

confirmed.title: Nothing in the suite cancels a job: FakeBackend.generate never polls should_cancel
confirmed.description: `grep -rn cancel tests/` returns exactly two hits: the should_cancel=None parameter in FakeBackend.generate and a comment in test_grid.py. The fake loops over steps calling only on_progress; it never calls should_cancel and never raises Cancelled, and no test posts to /api/jobs/{id}/cancel. So every branch of the cooperative-cancel design CLAUDE.md devotes a bullet to is unasserted: _finish's done_sent guard (which exists solely because cancellation gives two paths to the terminal event), cancel() finishing a still-queued job itself, the cancelled terminal status, `except Cancelled: break` (what keeps the images already written), shutdown() cancelling live jobs before the pool drains, and the ABC's stated contract that a backend must poll should_cancel - whose only in-repo double ignores it. All of these are correct today, so this is exposure rather than a live failure, but it is the largest unguarded surface in the codebase.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A regression in the cancel path ships with 135 green tests. If _finish's done_sent guard were dropped, cancelling a queued job would emit two terminal events; streamJob closes the source on the first, so the second is silently dropped and nothing looks wrong - until the ordering flips and a running job's done is the one swallowed, leaving the page stuck on 'Generating...' over an idle server. If `except Cancelled` became a raise, a cancelled overnight sweep would report status error with a traceback instead of 'Cancelled - kept 41 images'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the fake a cancellation point - `if should_cancel is not None and should_cancel(): raise Cancelled` inside the step loop - then two tests. (A) Running job: submit runs=4 with a slow fake, wait for the first image event, cancel, and assert the stream ends with exactly one done whose status is cancelled, whose images are non-empty, and that fewer than 4 requests reached the backend. (B) Queued job: submit two, cancel the second while the first runs, assert its stream yields exactly one event, done/cancelled. Write (A)'s synchronisation as a poll for the first image rather than a fixed sleep, and write the emit-once assertion at the JobManager level with a subscriber that stays attached past the first done - a reader that stops at the first event passes even with the guard removed.

confirmed.title: The load-on-first-generate path is untested: the fixture replaces main.jobs with a manager that has no ensure_loaded
confirmed.description: main.py wires the manager as `JobManager(backend, ensure_loaded)` and _run awaits that callable before taking the gate. CLAUDE.md makes this the single load path in the whole app, and DiffusersBackend.generate raises RuntimeError('model is not loaded') to enforce it. The `fake` fixture overwrites that wiring with `JobManager(backend)`, so self._ensure_loaded is None in every API test and the branch never runs; `grep -rn ensure_loaded tests/` returns nothing. The fake cannot detect the gap either - FakeBackend.generate renders regardless of self.loaded, so it has no double for the RuntimeError the real backend raises, and test_unload_is_refused_while_a_job_is_live ends asserting `not fake.loaded` in a state where a subsequent generate would succeed in the test and fail in production.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Deleting the ensure_loaded argument at main.py:80, or breaking ensure_loaded itself (the lock, the _load_state transitions, the error-to-short_error path), leaves all 135 tests passing while the documented primary user flow - 'The first POST /api/generate triggers a load' - 500s on the very first request, with /api/status still reporting unloaded. The load race CLAUDE.md says produced duplicate tracebacks also has no regression test.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the fake model the contract - track loads, set loaded in load(), and raise RuntimeError('model is not loaded') from generate() when it is False - and stop discarding the wiring: JobManager(backend, main.ensure_loaded) in the fixture (main.ensure_loaded reads the module-global backend, which the fixture has already patched). One test closes the hole: with FakeBackend(loaded=False), POST two generates back to back and assert both streams end done and fake.loads == 1.

confirmed.title: negative_prompt_supported is True is hard-coded against a profile that depends on KREA_MODEL_ID, so the suite fails on klein
confirmed.description: Line 147 asserts a literal for a value the server derives from settings.model_id: /api/status builds defaults from defaults_for(info['model_id']), and that id comes from KREA_MODEL_ID at import. Both klein profiles carry negative_prompt_supported: False - the whole point of the CLAUDE.md bullet. Every neighbouring test derives its expectation instead: test_a_bare_request_takes_the_checkpoints_profile and test_a_grid_says_which_cell_is_running both call defaults_for(settings.model_id). Line 147 is the only environment-coupled literal in the suite.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced on this checkout: `KREA_MODEL_ID=black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B uv run --group dev pytest -q` gives FAILED tests/test_api.py::test_status_says_whether_the_pipeline_takes_a_negative_prompt with 'assert False is True', 1 failed 134 passed; the nunchaku klein lite repo with KREA_QUANT=nunchaku fails identically. That second command is exactly the environment CLAUDE.md's Run section tells a WSL user to set up - `source wsl/env.sh` exports KREA_MODEL_ID into the shell - so a developer picking a klein lite repo gets a red suite that has nothing to do with their change, and the failure points at the wrong thing: it reads as 'the klein profile is broken' when the profile is right and the test is wrong.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the expectation the way line 113 does, and keep the assertion about what the test is actually for - that describe()'s answer overrides the profile's guess - by monkeypatching describe to return the negation. Better still, and it fixes the class rather than the instance: pin settings.model_id in the fixture with dataclasses.replace(...) the way conftest already pins db_path and outputs_dir, so no test in the suite reads KREA_MODEL_ID from the developer's shell.

confirmed.title: One generator per image, seeded seed+i, is asserted nowhere - the stubs take `generator` and throw it away
confirmed.description: CLAUDE.md makes this a headline invariant: 'A batch gets one generator per image, seeded seed + i ... One shared generator made the per-image seeds in the gallery unreproducible.' The backend implements it, and its comment notes that wrap_seed is used there and at the storage call on purpose. But grepping the tests for generator, initial_seed or manual_seed returns two hits, both stub-pipeline parameters that are accepted and discarded. Nothing asserts the number of generators, their seeds, or that those seeds equal what save_image records. The suite covers either side of the gap but not the join: test_seeds.py exercises wrap_seed in isolation, and test_a_sweep_reports_every_image_and_finishes asserts recorded seeds [7,8,9,10] and base seeds [7,9] - but FakeBackend builds no generators, so the assertion stops at the backend's front door.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified that the invariant holds today by driving the real DiffusersBackend.generate with a stub that captures generator: seed=2**63-2, num_images=4 yields [9223372036854775806, 9223372036854775807, 0, 1], matching wrap_seed(seed+i) exactly. A regression to a single scalar generator - the pre-2922c44 shape - leaves 135 tests green.
