In production image i of a 4-image batch would then depend on the batch size: save_image still writes seed+i into the filename, the PNG parameters block and the seed column, and Reuse still posts that seed back, but re-running it solo produces a different picture, with the gallery, the metadata and the UI all agreeing with each other and all disagreeing with the pixels.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Have the stub keep what it is handed and assert on it in test_schedule.py, where a stub already drives the real generate(): assert the list of `g.initial_seed()` equals `[wrap_seed(MAX_SEED - 1 + i) for i in range(4)]`. The base near MAX_SEED is the point - it pins the list-not-scalar shape, the seed+i offset and the shared wrap_seed in one assertion, using the same expression jobs._generate and generate.py use to build the row.

confirmed.title: Card tool buttons are gated on :hover alone - invisible to keyboard focus, absent on touch, and one of them is the only route to a run's contact sheet
confirmed.description: `.card .tools` is opacity 0, revealed only by `.card:hover .tools`. Grepping the whole stylesheet for focus-within or focus-visible returns nothing, so focus does not reveal them, and `.card .tools button` sets border: none with no :focus rule - opacity composites the whole subtree, the UA focus ring included. The four children stay in the tab order regardless: tool() creates plain buttons and card() appends four per card, and a full gallery page is 48 cards. This is the previous review's style.css:225 entry; only the missing delete confirm was fixed. New since that review: the sheet button added in 258920a is the only way in the UI to reach a run's contact sheet - it is the sole writer of `els.search.value = 'job:' + rec.job_id`, and job_id is rendered nowhere else (the lightbox meta line lists prompt, model, size, steps, CFG, mu, seed and duration but not the job), while filenames are timestamp-seed-uuid6, so the id is not there either.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A sighted keyboard user tabbing from the search box to 'Load more' passes through 192 invisible tab stops with no focus indicator; the first stop on each card is Reuse, which overwrites the prompt textarea, negative prompt, size, steps, CFG, mu and seed and smooth-scrolls to the top - an unrecoverable loss of a prompt being composed - and the fourth deletes the image and its PNG (the confirm dialog added in a93326e is all that stands in the way). On a touch device there is no hover at all, so the four per-card actions never appear. In both cases the sheet route to a run is unreachable and unrecoverable, because the job id it needs is never displayed: the user would have to read the PNG's job text chunk outside the app to type the search term by hand.
confirmed.suggested_fix: `.card:hover .tools, .card:focus-within .tools { opacity: 1 }` plus `.card .tools button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 1px }`. For touch, reveal the strip on a coarse pointer (`@media (hover: none)`) or move the actions into the lightbox's action row - which needs a Sheet button there anyway, since the lightbox is the only place a touch user can act on an image.

confirmed.title: The sticky control panel has no max-height, so on a laptop-height window Cancel and the whole grid section are pinned off-screen
confirmed.description: `.panel` is `position: sticky; top: 68px` with no max-height and no overflow, and `main` is a grid with align-items: start, so the panel's sticky containing block is the full-height gallery row: its top is held at y=68 for the whole scroll range and everything past 68 + viewportHeight is simply not on screen. The content has grown a long way since that rule was written - commits f859cc7/227641e appended the whole grid section (a summary, a hint, a 2-row textarea, four fields over three rows, a checkbox, a preview line and the Run grid button). Summing the stylesheet's own metrics at 330 px wide gives roughly 700-790 px closed and roughly 1000-1200 px with the grid section open, against ~640 px of usable height on a 1366x768 laptop; every textarea is resize: vertical, so the user can make it taller still. The order of what falls off is Generate, the progress row and its Cancel button, the error line, the grid section, Run grid. This is the previous review's unverified style.css:75 entry, still unfixed and now materially worse.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Start a 64-run sweep on a 1366x768 laptop with the grid section open, then scroll down to watch the images land: the Cancel button is off the bottom of the pinned panel and no amount of scrolling in that range brings it back - the run can only be stopped by scrolling to the very end of the gallery, where sticky finally releases, or by collapsing the grid section. The same geometry hides #error, so a failure reported by showError is written to an element the user never sees; on a 1080p display the grid workflow hits it too, with Run grid and the preview line that reports '480 cells, ~9h' or the axis error that just refused the submission both off-screen.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either stop sticking when the panel cannot fit - `@media (max-height: 900px) { .panel { position: static } }`, the side-effect-free option - or bound it: `max-height: calc(100vh - 86px); overflow-y: auto`. Note the second makes .panel a scroll container, which clips the absolutely-positioned .tip help panels (240 px wide, several lines tall; the Mu/Seeds/Resume ones would be cut off), so keep the tooltips usable by positioning them fixed from JS or moving them into a top-level layer. Either way also drop sticky inside the existing max-width: 900px block, where the single-column layout gives the panel no travel to use.

confirmed.title: The negative-prompt note renders at 3.0:1, and at 1.55:1 whenever the field is disabled - its default state on two of the three checkpoints
confirmed.description: `.field em { opacity: 0.65 }` applies to exactly one element, the neg-note em, whose text syncCfg writes. Composited, --muted #8b8b9a at 0.65 over --panel #131318 is #61616c: 3.03:1 at the 12 px of `.field > span`, below the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 requires under 18.5 px. When the field is off, `#negative-field.disabled { opacity: 0.45 }` multiplies with it - effective alpha 0.2925, rendered #36363e, 1.55:1. syncCfg turns the field off whenever CFG is at or below the threshold or the checkpoint takes no negative prompt, so on Krea 2 Turbo (profile CFG 0, threshold 0) and on FLUX.2 klein that is the state the page loads in. `.section > summary em { opacity: 0.6 }` is the same defect at 2.76:1. This is the previous review's style.css:83 cluster entry - the line moved, the rule did not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On klein the note is the only place the UI explains why the negative-prompt box is dead - '(this checkpoint takes no negative prompt)' - and it renders at 1.55:1, effectively invisible with reduced contrast sensitivity or on a screen in daylight. On Turbo the same slot carries the one instruction that would turn the field back on, '(needs CFG > 0 - ~2x slower)'. The 1.4.3 exemption for inactive components does not cover the 3.03:1 enabled case at all.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Drop the opacity and pick a token: `.field em { color: #a2a2b0 }` (5.9:1 on --panel) with the same for `.section > summary em`. For the disabled state, dim the textarea rather than the whole field - `#negative-field.disabled textarea { opacity: 0.45 }` - so the label and the note that explain the state stay legible. Related near-miss in the same file: .primary is #fff on --accent #7c5cff at 4.35:1, and its 14px/600 text is not WCAG large.

confirmed.title: Disk and download sizes understate both shipped checkpoints by 4-9 GB
confirmed.description: README:14 requires '~30 GB free disk for weights' and README:78 says 'The first generation downloads ~25 GB of weights'. Both numbers are the Krea 2 VRAM figure (CLAUDE.md 'needs ~25 GB in bf16', config.py 'none - full bfloat16, needs ~25GB VRAM') reused as a download size, and neither survived the move to FLUX as the default.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Measured on this machine's HF cache, where both checkpoints were fetched by this app's own from_pretrained (the snapshots contain exactly the folders named in model_index.json): FLUX.1-Krea-dev is 32 GiB - transformer 23,802,954,040 B in 3 shards, T5 text_encoder_2 9,524,648,584 B in 2 shards, plus 235 MB and 160 MB - and Krea-2-Turbo is 34 GiB. So the default checkpoint is ~31.4 GiB (~33.7 GB) on disk, past the stated ceiling, and 8-9 GB past the stated download; the 25 GB figure happens to be the transformer alone and omits the 8.9-9.5 GB text encoder the same call pulls. A user who provisions the documented 30 GB starts the app, waits tens of minutes, and dies out of disk inside the third transformer shard or the T5 encoder with a partial cache and no obvious cause.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Restate both numbers from the measured checkpoints and separate disk from VRAM: '~35 GB free disk per checkpoint (FLUX.1 Krea dev is 32 GiB, Krea 2 Turbo 34 GiB; the WSL Nunchaku Lite re-uploads are far smaller)' and 'downloads ~32 GB of weights for the default checkpoint'. Leave CLAUDE.md's ~25 GB alone - it is a VRAM figure and correct as such - but do not let the README borrow it again.

confirmed.title: The sheet prompt-label example is exactly the case promptLabels does not shorten
confirmed.description: README:314-319 promises 'The Prompt axis is labelled with only the words that vary - big grass, small dirt, or none for the cell that left the word out'. CLAUDE.md makes the same claim. promptLabels has two branches: equal word counts keep the differing positions (where 'big grass' comes from), unequal word counts strip only the shared head and the shared tail. A `none` value is what makes one prompt shorter, so the two behaviours are mutually exclusive - you can get 'big grass' or you can get 'none', never both in one run.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Running the exact algorithm over the six prompts of the README's own worked example (`{size} dog sitting on {ground}`, `size = big | small | none`, `ground = grass | dirt`) in the sorted order sheetValues produces, the output is identical to the input: head=0 (first words are big/dog/small), tail=0 (last words are dirt/grass), so every one of the six column headers reads the whole sentence - the unreadable full-sentence header the section says it avoids. Without the none value the same grid gives big dirt, big grass, small dirt, small grass as documented; CLAUDE.md's own single-variable example also reproduces.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Either narrow the prose or widen the code. Docs-only: say the labels keep the words that vary when every prompt has the same word count, and that a none value falls back to trimming the shared head and tail - which strips nothing when a second variable also varies. Code fix, which keeps both documents true: in the unequal-length branch, align on the shared words rather than only head and tail (drop every position present and identical in all prompts after an LCS alignment), yielding 'big grass' / 'small dirt' / 'none grass' for the README's example.

confirmed.title: cfg_threshold()'s 'has negative_prompt -> 0.0' branch is a Krea2-only rule applied to every pipeline, and it makes the loaded answer worse than the unloaded guess
confirmed.description: cfg_threshold() is three-way: true_cfg_scale present -> 1.0, else negative_prompt present -> 0.0, else 1.0. The middle branch generalises one fact about Krea2Pipeline (do_classifier_free_guidance is `self._guidance_scale > 0`) into 'any pipeline that takes a negative prompt guides from 0'. Parsing every pipeline_*.py in diffusers 0.40, 131 pipeline classes have negative_prompt, no true_cfg_scale and an explicit do_classifier_free_guidance property; 122 of them gate at > 1 and only 9 gate at > 0 (Krea2Pipeline and the seven ZImage classes).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Run through the backend's own code with the real signatures, StableDiffusion3Pipeline, StableDiffusionXLPipeline, ChromaPipeline and Lumina2Pipeline all answer cfg_threshold 0.0 while their own gate is `guidance_scale > 1`. The inversion is the sharp part: model_defaults._FALLBACK guesses cfg_threshold 1.0 for an unrecognised checkpoint, which is right, and main.status() then overwrites that correct guess with the loaded pipeline's 0.0 - so loading the model makes /api/status less accurate than it was before the load. With KREA_MODEL_ID pointed at SD3.5 the UI ungreys the negative prompt at CFG 0.5, the tooltip reads 'Above 0 the negative prompt applies', and generate() passes a negative prompt to a pipeline whose guidance branch is off - which storage then records as having run. generate.py escapes this because the CLI uses the profile guess, so terminal and browser disagree about the same run. The three catalogue families are all answered correctly, so this only bites off-catalogue.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Ask the pipeline where its own gate is rather than inferring it from a parameter name: the property reads only _guidance_scale, so it can be evaluated at 1.0 once at load time and cached beside _call_params, with cfg_threshold becoming true_cfg_scale -> 1.0, else 0.0 if the gate fires at 1.0 else 1.0. That answers Krea2 0.0, klein 1.0, FLUX.1 1.0 and SD3/SDXL/Chroma/Lumina2 1.0. If the probe is too clever for taste, a literal set of pipeline class names defaulting to 1.0 fixes the same 122 cases. Either way correct the CLAUDE.md bullet whose stated rule encodes the wrong generalisation, and add the missing stub case (negative_prompt with a > 1 gate) beside tests/test_klein.py's.

confirmed.title: A *.png.part left by a failed or killed encode is invisible to summarise() and swept by nothing, so it never goes away
confirmed.description: This is the residue of the previous review's fix for the orphan-sweep collision. The .part scheme works exactly as intended for a live encode, but nothing ever collects a partial that is not live. `image.save(partial, ...)` sits outside the try that begins on the next line, so the `except BaseException: _unlink(partial)` guard covers only the INSERT and the rename; a failure or interruption during the ~240 ms encode leaves the file behind. Nothing else looks for it, and that is deliberate for the live case but total: summarise() globs *.png so files_on_disk and bytes_on_disk do not count it, clear_history's orphan sweep globs *.png so --yes does not delete it, and delete_image only unlinks a tracked filename. `grep -rn '\.part' backend/` finds only the sites in save_image and a clear_history comment; there is no sweep anywhere.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C or a crash during a 4 MP encode, or image.save raising because the disk filled or outputs_dir was moved, leaves a multi-megabyte .png.part in outputs/ forever. `python -m backend.clear --yes` then reports '0 PNG files, 0 B' for that space and deletes nothing - and clear.py's own early return on records == 0 and files_on_disk == 0 prints 'Nothing to clear.' over a directory that is not empty. A later run of the same grid re-renders the cell (resume keys on the committed row, which never existed) and can leave another; over a life of interrupted overnight sweeps the directory silently accumulates them.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Two independent halves. (1) Put the encode inside the existing cleanup so a failed image.save tidies after itself. (2) Make the leftovers visible and collectable: add a stale_partials count and its bytes to summarise() from `outputs_dir.glob('*.png.part')`, print it in clear.py's preview beside the orphan line and in its 'Nothing to clear' guard, and sweep partials older than a settle window (a live encode is ~240 ms old, so an hour has four orders of magnitude of slack, and nothing streams a .part) from clear_history - as a separate count, or tests/test_gallery.py's orphans assertion breaks. Do not add *.png.part to the unconditional glob: that reopens the race the .part naming closed. Both CLAUDE.md and README state the sweep does not touch a .png.part flatly, so both sentences need the age qualifier in the same change.

confirmed.title: clear_history snapshots `keep` before the orphan glob, so it deletes the PNG of a row committed in between
confirmed.description: `clear_history` reads the surviving filenames at line 505 and only then globs and unlinks. save_image commits its row and then renames `<name>.png.part` into `<name>.png`, so any image whose row commits after the keep read but whose rename lands before the glob observes it is seen as untracked and deleted, while its row survives. The comment at 502-504 - 'a clear during a sweep can no longer delete one out from under it' - is true for the encode window and false for the commit-to-glob window, which spans the whole glob and unlink loop (seconds on a directory of thousands of files). summarise() has the identical inversion. This is the surviving half of the previous review's storage.py:265 entry; the .part half landed, this one did not, and the prior fix note, the code comment and README all assert a guarantee the code does not provide.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced by wrapping storage._tracked_files so one save_image runs immediately after the snapshot: clear_history returns records 1, files 1, orphans 1, and the new image ends with its row still in the gallery and its PNG gone from disk. clear.py's docstring says it is safe to run while the server is up; run `python -m backend.clear --yes` during an overnight sweep and an image the sweep finishes inside the sweep's own orphan loop has its PNG deleted while the row stays. The gallery then shows a card whose /outputs URL 404s forever - no future orphan sweep can help, since there is no file, and no clear reports it, because summarise() counts rows and files separately. The window is ~1000x narrower than before the .part fix, so this is rare rather than routine, but silent and unrecoverable when it hits.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Materialise the glob before reading keep, so the snapshot is strictly newer than every file it judges - a file the glob saw was renamed after its row committed, so a keep read afterwards necessarily contains it. Apply the same reorder in summarise(). A regression test can drive it the way the reproduction did: patch _tracked_files to commit one save_image on its way out, then assert the new record's file still exists.

confirmed.title: step_cost_ms measures the previous checkpoint's rows, so /api/grid/preview's duration estimate is wrong after a model switch
confirmed.description: step_cost_ms() picks the last 20 gallery rows matching only width, height, steps > 0 and duration_ms > 0. It does not filter on model_id, so the median ms-per-step it returns can come entirely from a checkpoint that is no longer loaded, and main.preview_grid multiplies that by the grid's total step count and publishes it as GridPreview.seconds. The same request, in the same handler, already knows better: _expand's resume path calls completed_cells(..., settings.model_id) and that query does filter on model_id. One of the two functions that read gallery rows on behalf of a grid preview keys on the checkpoint and the other does not.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The checkpoints this project ships disagree about per-step cost by roughly 2x at the same resolution: from CLAUDE.md's own measurements on the 5080 under Nunchaku NVFP4, FLUX.2 klein renders 1 MP in 4.0 s at 4 steps = 1000 ms/step, while Krea 2 Turbo renders 1 MP in 15 s at 8 steps = 1875 ms/step. A user who renders with klein at 1024x1024, then restarts on Turbo and opens the grid panel, is quoted a duration built from klein's 1000 ms/step: a 1024-image grid at 8 steps is reported as about 2h 20m and actually takes about 4h 30m. The error is silent and optimistic, and None - 'no rows, promise nothing' - is the designed answer for exactly this situation, but the query cannot tell the two cases apart. Changing KREA_QUANT moves it further, and neither quantization nor offload is recorded in the images table at all.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add model_id to the predicate and pass settings.model_id from main.py's call. A fresh checkpoint then correctly returns None until it has rendered something at that size, which the preview already handles. Update the CLAUDE.md bullet describing the estimate as 'measured from recent gallery rows at the same size' to say 'at the same size on the same checkpoint'.

confirmed.title: The lightbox is a modal overlay with no dialog role, no focus move, no focus trap and no focus restore
confirmed.description: renderLightbox() opens the overlay with the single line `els.lightbox.hidden = false;` and closeLightbox() hides it again. Nothing else happens: grepping app.js for focus(), activeElement, aria or role returns no matches at all, and index.html:217 is a plain div with no role=dialog, no aria-modal, and no inert/aria-hidden on main. Three consequences follow from those lines: focus stays where the click left it, so a screen reader is told nothing opened; the overlay div is the last element in the document, after </main>, so a virtual cursor in the gallery has no way to know the content now covering the page exists; and Tab from that stale focus walks the page behind the 0.92-opaque overlay, where Enter activates controls invisibly. #lb-img also keeps the literal alt="" from index.html - renderLightbox sets .src but never .alt - so the one image the dialog exists to show is marked decorative. This is the previous review's app.js:423/415 cluster, unfixed; Escape does close the overlay and Delete now confirms, so the specific blind-delete story is out of date.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Click a card, then Tab: focus is on the Unload button, invisible behind the backdrop, and Enter there POSTs /api/model/unload - which succeeds whenever no job is running, dropping the checkpoint from VRAM with no visible cause and costing a multi-minute reload on the next Generate. Continuing to Tab types into the prompt box behind the overlay. On close, focus is still wherever it was, so a user who opened image 30 of a page is returned to the top of the tab order rather than to that card.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Smallest complete version: make it a real `<dialog>` and use showModal()/close(), which supplies the focus trap, top-layer stacking, background inertness and focus restore for free (adjust the backdrop click and drop the manual Escape branch, keep the arrows). By hand: role=dialog aria-modal=true with an aria-label, stash document.activeElement in openLightbox and focus #lb-close, restore it in closeLightbox, and either trap Tab over the five controls or set `main.inert = true` while open. Also set `els.lbImg.alt = rec.prompt` beside the src and clear it on close.

confirmed.title: No live region anywhere: errors, progress and model status change silently
confirmed.description: `grep -n 'aria-\|role=' web/index.html` matches only the ten help badges. Every piece of dynamically-written status text is an inert element: the error paragraph written by showError(), the progress-text span written on every progress event, the progress bar (a width-percentage div with no role=progressbar and no aria-valuenow), the status-text span rewritten every 3 s by refreshStatus, plus #cell-note, #grid-preview and #sheet-note. None is announced. This is the previous review's index.html:58 cluster entry, unfixed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user presses Generate with an empty prompt: startJob returns after showError('Enter a prompt first.'), the button does not change, nothing is announced, and the app appears to have ignored the keypress. With a prompt, the same user gets no announcement that the job queued, that weights are loading (minutes), that a step counter is moving, that images landed, or that the run finished or errored - the only feedback is the button text changing on a button that is disabled and no longer focused.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add role=alert to the error paragraph (it announces when it goes from hidden to shown, which is exactly showError's pattern) - but set hidden=false before assigning textContent, since [hidden]{display:none!important} means the text is otherwise written into a display:none node. role=status on #progress-text, role=progressbar with aria-valuemin/max on the bar and aria-valuenow set alongside style.width, and aria-live=polite on #status-text guarded by a change check, since it is assigned unconditionally every 3 s. Throttle the progress region to run boundaries so it does not chatter once per step.

confirmed.title: Icon-only buttons are named by their glyph; the `title` given to tool() is never used as the accessible name
confirmed.description: tool(label, title, onClick) sets textContent to the glyph and title to the description. Per accname step 2F a button takes its name from its subtree contents, and the tooltip step is only reached when that yields an empty string - so the computed names of the card tools are the glyphs themselves and 'Reuse settings', 'Show this run as a sheet', 'Favorite' and 'Delete' are never exposed. The same shape is hand-written in index.html for the dice button, the lightbox close and the two lightbox arrows, whose titles are likewise discarded. The arrow and delete glyphs are not in NVDA's default English symbol dictionary at punctuation level 'some', so they announce as a bare 'button'. This is the previous review's app.js:379 cluster entry, unfixed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A screen-reader user tabbing a gallery card hears 'button, button, star, button' - four unlabelled controls, the last of which deletes the image and its file from disk. In the lightbox the two navigation arrows and the close control are equally anonymous, so paging through a 480-image grid run is guesswork. The dice button announces as 'game die', which does not say it clears the seed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give each button an aria-label as well as the glyph and mark the glyph decorative: `b.setAttribute('aria-label', title)` alone overrides the content name. Add aria-label to the four hand-written buttons in index.html matching their existing titles. For the star, update the label alongside the glyph in setFavorite so it says Favourite/Unfavourite rather than reading a filled star as an action.

confirmed.title: SHEET_PAGE and the gallery's le=1024 are hard-wired to the default of the tunable KREA_MAX_GRID_IMAGES
confirmed.description: Three numbers have to agree and only one is configurable: config.py's `max_grid_images = int(os.getenv('KREA_MAX_GRID_IMAGES', '1024'))`, documented in the README as a user-settable knob; `const SHEET_PAGE = 1024` in app.js, used as the gallery limit while sheetMode is on; and `limit: int = Query(48, ge=1, le=1024)` in main.py. CLAUDE.md states the contract the sheet depends on - 'It asks for the whole run in one page because a matrix with a page boundary through it is a puzzle' - which holds only while max_grid_images <= SHEET_PAGE <= 1024, and nothing states or checks it. The sheet's own escape hatch is closed too: `els.more.hidden = sheetMode || offset >= total`, so Load more is unconditionally hidden in sheet mode, and rows come back id DESC, so the page that is kept is the newest 1024 - the earliest seeds, which are the outermost loop, are the ones dropped.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Set KREA_MAX_GRID_IMAGES=2000 (a documented setting) and queue a 2000-image grid overnight. Next morning, search job:<id> and click Sheet: the request is limit=1024, the sheet lays out only the newest 1024 images, the note reads 'N of 1024 loaded - 2000 match the search', and the matrix is missing whole rows of the seed axis with no control that can reach them. Raising SHEET_PAGE to 2048 to compensate makes every sheet request a 422 - 'limit: Input should be less than or equal to 1024' - because the second copy of the number was never touched.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the ceiling one value the client can read: publish max_grid_images (and a max page if the cap should stay independent) on /api/status and have app.js use it in place of the literal, and derive Query's le from settings. Failing that, at minimum stop hiding Load more in sheet mode so a truncated sheet can be completed, and have renderSheet say the matrix is incomplete rather than only counting rows.

confirmed.title: A sweep that rendered every one of its images is reported as 'cancelled'
confirmed.description: `job.status = "cancelled" if job.cancel_requested else "done"` reads the request flag rather than whether the run actually stopped early. _generate observes the flag only at the top of each cell and the backend polls it only at step boundaries, so a cancel that lands after the final step - during the VAE decode, during the ~240 ms PNG encode and INSERT per image, or in the gap between the executor future resolving and _run resuming on the loop - changes nothing about what ran but still flips the terminal status. cancel() accepts any non-terminal job, and shutdown() sets the same flag on every active job, so a Ctrl-C in that window mislabels too. This is the previous review's unverified jobs.py:161 entry, still unfixed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced deterministically with a 2-run sweep and a cancel posted from inside save_image while the second and last image is being written: backend calls 2, images produced 2, final status cancelled. The user hits Cancel as the last image of a long sweep lands; everything they asked for was rendered, but the terminal SSE event carries cancelled, so the UI shows 'Cancelled - kept 64 images.' instead of finishing normally, GET /api/jobs/{id} reports cancelled for a run that completed, and any script treating cancelled as 'incomplete, resume it' re-queues a grid with nothing left to do (which the resume path then answers 409).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Report what actually happened rather than what was asked: have _generate return True from its two break paths and False after the loop completes, then `job.status = 'cancelled' if stopped else 'done'`. Equivalently, compare the number of completed cells with len(job.cells).

confirmed.title: _run overwrites a job's terminal status after `done` has already been sent with a different one
confirmed.description: cancel() finishes a still-queued job on the spot: status becomes cancelled, _finish sets done_sent and emits the terminal SSE event. But that job's _run task is still alive, parked in `await self._ensure_loaded()`. If the load then fails, the except clause runs unconditionally - status error, error text, _finish - and _finish correctly no-ops on done_sent, so the event is suppressed while the state is silently rewritten. The sibling branch nine lines down was hardened against exactly this (it checks job.cancel_requested before assigning); this one was not. This is the previous review's unverified jobs.py:146 entry, half fixed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a JobManager wired to an ensure_loaded that sleeps and then raises a gated-repo 403: the cancel endpoint says cancelled, the SSE terminal event says done/cancelled, and the REST snapshot afterwards says error with a load traceback. Two API surfaces then disagree about the same job permanently: a client that drives the API without a stream - curl, /docs, any submit-then-poll script - reads error for a job the user deliberately stopped and treats it as a failure to retry. The same shape applies to any exception out of ensure_loaded (gated repo, no CUDA, HF network failure), which is precisely when a user is most likely to cancel rather than wait.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the terminal write conditional the way the sibling branch already is, or better, move it into _finish so there is one place that can turn a job terminal: `_finish(loop, job, status=None, error=None)` returning early on done_sent and assigning only when it does not. Every status transition then goes through the same guard.

confirmed.title: _MAX_SWEEP_SPAN covers runs x num_images but not a grid's 256-seed axis, so a drawn seed can still leave the JSON-exact range
confirmed.description: _MAX_SWEEP_SPAN is documented as 'the largest offset a single request can add to its base seed: runs steps the seed by num_images each time, and both are capped in GenerateRequest', and RANDOM_SEED_MAX subtracts it so every seed derived from a random draw stays inside the exactly-representable range - the whole reason the module exists. A grid does not step by runs: GridRequest rejects runs != 1 and steps by `seeds`, capped at 256 in GridRequest rather than 64, with jobs._generate adding the per-image offset on top. The reachable offset is `seeds * num_images - 1`, bounded in practice by max_grid_images (1024 by default, env-overridable), i.e. 1023 - double the 511 reserved, and 2047 if the ceiling is raised. tests/test_seeds.py asserts the invariant with the same wrong bound: it computes the span from runs and num_images only, so it passes while the grid path can walk past 2**53-1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A grid with no explicit seed, 128 seeds and batch 8 whose random base lands in the top ~1000 values of the draw range: the last cells' per-image seeds exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, come back from res.json() rounded, and Reuse then posts a seed one or two away from the one save_image wrote into the PNG and the filename - disk right, UI wrong, silent, and the exact failure the constant exists to prevent. Honest about the odds: the draw has to land within ~1000 of the top of a 2**53 range, so this is ~1e-13 per grid and nobody will hit it. The finding is that the constant no longer means what its comment says, and the next cap raised - seeds, num_images, or a new axis - has no reason to notice.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the span from every cap that can multiply a base seed rather than from two of them - `max(MAX_RUNS, MAX_GRID_SEEDS) * MAX_BATCH`, or the grid ceiling - and stop hand-maintaining the list: define the three caps in seeds.py (or a tiny shared limits module) and have GenerateRequest/GridRequest use them as their le= values, since seeds.py must not import schemas. Then widen tests/test_seeds.py to take GridRequest.seeds into account; it is currently the thing certifying the wrong bound.

confirmed.title: An unrecognised KREA_QUANT or KREA_OFFLOAD silently falls through to full bf16 / no offload while /api/status echoes the value back
confirmed.description: Still open from the previous review's unverified list. Nothing validates either value: _quantization_config returns None for anything outside the two torchao backends and nunchaku, with no log line - while the two real fall-throughs next to it do log - and load()'s offload block is an if/elif/else whose else is 'keep everything resident'. config.py reads both with a bare os.getenv and no check, and describe() reports them verbatim, so /api/status and the CLI header repeat the typo back as if it had been applied. The menu and the flags are safe (argparse choices), but the environment variables are the documented interface and wsl/env.sh sets KREA_QUANT through a `${KREA_QUANT:-nunchaku}` default, so a value already exported in the shell wins silently. Three documented paths bypass the menu entirely: `--defaults`, any non-tty start, and backend.generate without an explicit --quant.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `export KREA_OFFLOAD=cpu` (a natural guess for the accelerate-style name; the real key is `model`) loads everything resident. Per CLAUDE.md's own measurements that is 14.7 GiB at 1 MP and 18.7 GiB at 2 MP on a 16 GB card, with the WDDM driver spilling into system RAM: 26 s and 72 s instead of 15 s and 24 s, while /api/status reports offload 'cpu' throughout so nothing points at the cause. `export KREA_QUANT=fp16` - or 'float8', the spelling this module's own docstring and the README use in prose - is worse: no preflight and no torchao mapping run, the 25 GB bf16 checkpoint loads without complaint after several minutes, and the first image OOMs, which is exactly the late failure _nunchaku_preflight was written to prevent for the other mode.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Validate at import, next to the DIFFUSERS_TRUST_REMOTE_KERNELS block in config.py, where the failure is one line at startup rather than minutes into a download. The vocabularies already exist as data in launch.QUANTIZATIONS/OFFLOADS, but config must not import launch's dependency graph - lift the two tuples into a tiny module both read, then raise SystemExit naming the allowed values. A test in the existing _settings_in_subprocess style pins it. Failing that, an else-branch log.warning on the offload chain and on the quantization fall-through at least puts it in the log.

confirmed.title: _migrate's once-per-process flag defeats the per-connection recovery _connect was written for
confirmed.description: _connect re-checks for the images table on every connection, and its comment names why: 'the file can disappear under a running server - deleted by hand, moved, restored from a backup. Without this the gallery 500s on every request until restart. The lookup is a sqlite_master hit, cheap enough to pay per connection.' _migrate is called on the very next line but guards itself with a module-level flag, so the column check is paid once per process. The two guards therefore disagree about lifetime, and the case they disagree on is exactly the one _connect's comment calls out: if the file dropped in place is an older gallery without job_id, _connect sees images present and skips _SCHEMA, _migrate returns immediately, and the missing column is never added. PRAGMA table_info is no more expensive than the sqlite_master lookup already paid. The test suite already works around the flag's process lifetime with a monkeypatch reset.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Server running against the current krea.db, so _migrated is True. The user restores last week's krea.db over it - the scenario storage.py's comment exists to survive. Every subsequent save_image raises `sqlite3.OperationalError: table images has no column named job_id` from the INSERT; the except handler deletes the .png.part, so the rendered image is thrown away, and jobs._run marks the job error and abandons the rest of the sweep. /api/gallery still works (SELECT * does not need the column), so the failure looks like a generation bug rather than a schema one, and it persists until the server is restarted.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Drop the flag and let the check ride with _connect's existing per-connection lookup, or scope the flag to 'this database' rather than 'this process' by keying it on settings.db_path. Either way the tests can then drop their _migrated reset.

confirmed.title: An unguarded vacuum() between the delete and its report loses the counts, and exit 1 cannot be told from 'aborted'
confirmed.description: main() has no exception handling anywhere. Line 108 commits the destructive work - clear_history DELETEs the rows and unlinks the files - and line 109 then runs storage.vacuum(), a pure space optimisation, before the report at 111-118 that is the only record of what was destroyed. vacuum() opens its own connection and runs VACUUM, which needs an exclusive lock and can raise; verified locally that with another connection holding a write transaction it raises 'database is locked' after the busy timeout. A DB on a network or 9P path - the configuration CLAUDE.md warns about - and a full disk are the other realistic raisers. When it raises, the traceback escapes main(), Python exits 1, and 1 is also what the two abort paths return - the paths that delete nothing. This is the previous review's unverified clear.py:100 entry, half fixed: the unlink loops now go through storage._unlink, which swallows OSError; the report-and-exit-code half moved from the unlinks to vacuum() and is still live.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `uv run python -m backend.clear --yes` on a 4021-image gallery with the WSL server mid-INSERT, or a DB path SQLite cannot lock: the rows and 4021 PNGs are gone, and the user sees `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` with a traceback instead of 'Deleted 4021 record(s), 4021 file(s).' A wrapper script reading the exit code gets 1 and cannot distinguish that from the user typing anything other than 'clear' at the confirmation, which deletes nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Report first, then vacuum, and treat vacuum as best-effort (catch sqlite3.Error and print a note to stderr). Give the destructive step its own failure code - wrap the clear_history call and return 3 - leaving 1 for 'aborted, nothing deleted', and document both in the README's exit-status sentence, which currently covers only generate.py.

confirmed.title: The 'negative prompt ignored' note is computed from the base CFG, so a --grid-cfg run reports it backwards
confirmed.description: The block deciding whether to annotate the negative prompt with '[ignored: CFG is at or below N]' uses request.guidance_scale - the single base value from --cfg or the profile. It runs before the CFG axis is printed, and nothing reconciles the two: in a --grid-cfg run the base value is not what any cell necessarily uses. The resolved-settings block is the whole point of --dry-run and the header of every overnight log, and the note is the one line in it that is not derived from the cells actually queued.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Both directions verified with --dry-run. `generate "x" -n blurry --cfg 0.5 --grid-cfg 2,3` prints 'negative : blurry  [ignored: CFG is at or below 1]' above 'CFG : 2, 3' - every cell of that run applies the negative prompt and the CLI says it is ignored. The inverse, `generate "x" -n blurry --grid-cfg 0,1,3.5`, prints no warning while two of three cells drop it. A user sweeping CFG across the threshold - the most obvious use of --grid-cfg on FLUX, since the threshold is where the negative prompt starts working - reads the header, believes their negative prompt is dead, drops -n and re-runs a night that was already correct.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the note from the resolved axis instead of the base: hoist the `values` computation above the negative-prompt print and branch on how many of `values['guidance_scale']` exceed the threshold - none, some, or all. For a non-grid run the list is a single value and the text is exactly what it prints today.

confirmed.title: --no-mu silently swallows an explicit --mu instead of being rejected as a conflict
confirmed.description: `mu = None if args.no_mu else (args.mu if args.mu is not None else profile['mu'])` - --no-mu short-circuits before args.mu is looked at, and argparse is given no mutual-exclusion group, so `--mu 1.15 --no-mu` parses cleanly and runs with no shift at all. Every other contradiction in this parser is caught and named: --width with --aspect, --width without --height, --runs with --grid-*, --resume without --seed. This is the previous review's unverified generate.py:183 entry, unfixed; confirmed that `--mu 3 --no-mu --dry-run` prints 'sampling : 28 steps, CFG 3.5, mu -'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Turbo, mu is part of the reproduction set and a different mu is a different image. A shell-history line or a script that grew --no-mu while an earlier --mu 1.4 stayed on renders a whole overnight sweep at the pipeline's own shift and records mu NULL for all of it; there is no error and, under --quiet, no printed settings block to notice it in. Partly self-limiting: without --quiet the resolved 'mu -' is printed before the run starts.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Put them in a mutually exclusive group in _build_parser; argparse then exits 2 with 'argument --no-mu: not allowed with argument --mu', matching the exit code the README already documents for bad arguments, and documents itself in --help. Line 200 needs no change.

confirmed.title: Ctrl-C during the weight load promises to stop 'at the end of this step' and then does nothing for minutes
confirmed.description: The SIGINT handler is installed before backend.load(). During the load there is no step and no should_cancel poll: the first Ctrl-C only sets `stop` and prints 'cancelling at the end of this step (Ctrl-C again to force)...'. load() then runs to completion - minutes on a warm cache, far longer on a cold one downloading 12-25 GB - and only then does `if stop: break` fire, so the process finishes the entire load, generates nothing, prints '0/N image(s)' and exits 130. The message is the sweep's message shown in a phase where it cannot be true. This is the previous review's unverified generate.py:253 entry, unfixed. The escape works: a second Ctrl-C raises KeyboardInterrupt from the handler, caught with 'Interrupted during load; nothing generated.' and 130 - so the defect is the wrong first message, not an unkillable process.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user who mistypes a prompt and hits Ctrl-C ten seconds into a cold-cache load reads 'cancelling at the end of this step', waits for the cancel to land, and sits through the whole download before the process exits having drawn nothing. The correct action - hit Ctrl-C again - is described by the parenthetical as 'force', which reads like something that risks a half-written file rather than the only way out.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track the phase and say the true thing: set a `loading` flag around backend.load() and branch in _on_sigint. Better still, drop the two-press requirement in the load phase - while loading, re-raise immediately, which the existing except already turns into 'Interrupted during load; nothing generated.' and exit 130. There is nothing in a load worth finishing after a cancel. Amend the module docstring, which promises the two-stage behaviour unconditionally.

confirmed.title: The CLI's grid path prints the raw pydantic blob for an out-of-range axis, though the browser and the CLI's own base-request path strip it
confirmed.description: generate.py has two error funnels for the same class of failure. The first exists precisely because 'Pydantic's own repr is several lines of type/url noise per field' and unpacks exc.errors() into one line per field. The second wraps grid.expand() and does `print(exc, file=sys.stderr)` - but grid.expand is where a bad axis actually surfaces, because every cell is constructed as a real GenerateRequest and a value outside the schema raises ValidationError, a ValueError subclass. The same knowledge is written three times (main._detail, generate.py's first handler, and not at all at the third site) and the one place it is missing is the grid path - the path CLAUDE.md says exists so 'an axis value outside the schema fails at submit with the schema's own message rather than sixty images in'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Measured at HEAD: `uv run python -m backend.generate "a dog" --grid-steps 90-120x10 --dry-run` prints four lines - '1 validation error for GenerateRequest', 'steps', 'Input should be less than or equal to 100 [type=less_than_equal, input_value=110, input_type=int]' and a pydantic docs URL - where the browser gets the single line 'steps: Input should be less than or equal to 100' from main._detail, whose docstring names this exact case. In a redirected overnight log it is four lines of noise around the one sentence that matters.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Lift the existing formatter out of main.py into a shared helper (backend/schemas.py or a small backend/errors.py) and use it in all three places, so main.py stops keeping its own copy.

confirmed.title: clear.py can neither report nor remove a stale *.png.part, so an interrupted encode leaks a file forever
confirmed.description: CLAUDE.md describes clear.py as the thing that 'deletes rows, their PNGs and any orphans', and it is the only tool in the repo that collects untracked files. It cannot see or touch *.png.part: summarise() globs *.png for both files_on_disk and orphan_files, and clear_history's orphan sweep globs *.png - deliberately, and tests/test_gallery.py pins that, because an in-flight write must survive a concurrent clear. The gap is stale partials, not in-flight ones; see the storage.py:184 entry for the write-side half.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Power cut during an overnight sweep, or a disk that fills mid-encode: 2-8 MB per event sits in outputs/ permanently. The user runs `python -m backend.clear --yes` to reclaim space, gets 'Deleted 4021 record(s), 4021 file(s).' and 'Remaining: 0 record(s), 0 file(s), 0.0 B' - a summary that is arithmetically consistent and factually wrong, because files_on_disk counted only *.png. `ls` still shows the partials and nothing in the tool explains them.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Sweep partials by age, which is safe here in a way the previous review's rejected mtime heuristic was not: a .png.part is never served, so nothing can hold one open except the encode writing it. Return it as a fourth count and name it in clear.py's report and preview, so a leak is visible even when the sweep declines to remove a recent one. Extend tests/test_gallery.py to keep asserting that a fresh partial survives while a back-dated one goes.

confirmed.title: resumeActiveJob attaches to the newest live job, so an older running sweep stays uncancellable
confirmed.description: GET /api/jobs returns every non-terminal job in submission order. resumeActiveJob takes `active[active.length - 1]` - the newest, which when two jobs are live is the queued one, not the one holding the gate - and binds currentJob to it, which is what cancelJob targets. The older, actually-running job is left with no id anywhere in the page: exactly the state GET /api/jobs was added to fix.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two tabs, both opened before anything was running. Tab A submits a 480-cell grid. Tab B's resumeActiveJob already ran at load and found nothing, so the user clicks Generate there and job H queues behind the grid. Reload either tab: both reattach to H, the panel reads 'waiting for the job ahead...', and Cancel stops H. The grid keeps the GPU for hours with no reachable id - Unload answers 409 - and only killing the server stops it. Same end state after the five-failure give-up path nulls currentJob and the user starts a second job.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Prefer the job that is actually running: `const job = active.find((j) => j.status === 'running') ?? active[active.length - 1];`. Better still, render a one-line 'N more queued' note from active.length so the second job is visible; cancelling it needs only its id, which the list carries.

confirmed.title: Size presets, Reuse and the dice button change controls without firing `input`, so the grid preview keeps stale numbers
confirmed.description: The grid preview is wired only to input events on eight fields, with the comment 'both the size and the batch move the totals'. Assigning .value from script fires no input event, and three code paths do exactly that without calling schedulePreview(): choose() (the preset buttons, the primary way sizes get set), reuse() (which rewrites prompt, size, steps, CFG, mu and seed in one go) and the dice handler (which clears the seed). previewGrid posts gridPayload(), whose width and height feed storage.step_cost_ms on the server, so the estimate is size-dependent.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Open the grid panel with a 1 MP preset: '480 images - ... - about 3h'. Click the 4 MP pill. The panel still says about 3h for a run that will take roughly four times that, and nothing refreshes it until an unrelated keystroke lands in one of the eight wired fields. After Reuse the preview describes the settings from before the reuse - including the resolved prompt lines, which is the part of a prompt grid the preview exists to show. Clicking the dice with Resume ticked leaves the preview showing a valid grid when the request would now 422 for want of a seed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call schedulePreview() at the end of choose(), at the end of reuse() alongside the existing sync calls, and in the dice handler. Or route every programmatic write through one helper that dispatches a bubbling input event, so syncSize, ownControls and schedulePreview all see it and no future setter can forget one.

confirmed.title: OFFSET paging over a table the generation thread is inserting into duplicates cards and hides the same number of older images
confirmed.description: _page fetches with ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ? and the client tracks a running offset. New rows arrive at the top of that ordering - the generation thread calls save_image for every image of a sweep, and each INSERT shifts every previously-fetched row one place down. The client appends without deduplicating, so a repeat is a second card, and openLightbox resolves it through indexOf, which finds the first copy. This is distinct from the previous review's app.js:325 entry, which has been fixed: that guard serialises the caller but does nothing about rows moving underneath a stable offset. _page's COUNT and SELECT are also two separate statements on a connection that starts no read transaction, so total can be one page out of step with the rows returned.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Leave the gallery open during a 64-run sweep and click Load more after three images have landed. Page 2 is fetched at OFFSET 48 of a list that now has three new rows at the front, so the last three cards of page 1 reappear as the first three of page 2, and three older images are skipped and never shown until something calls resetGallery(). The lightbox's next/prev then walks over the duplicates and stops early relative to the count badge.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Switch to keyset paging, which is immune to inserts at the head: take a before_id instead of an offset (`... AND id < ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ?`) and have the client carry the last id it saw. If offset paging is worth keeping for the sheet's single big page, at minimum dedupe by id on the client before the push, so a shifted page cannot produce two cards for one image.

confirmed.title: The unload guard covers jobs but not loads: an unload issued during a load waits out the whole load, then throws it away
confirmed.description: unload_model refuses while a job is live but says nothing about a load. backend.unload() takes part in none of the loading coordination: ensure_loaded holds the module-level _load_lock across its whole load and DiffusersBackend.load() holds self._lock across from_pretrained, but unload() only takes self._lock - so the unload thread blocks there until the load finishes, then immediately discards the pipeline that load just built. CLAUDE.md asserts 'Loading happens in exactly one place: main.ensure_loaded(), which holds an asyncio lock across the whole load', which reads as coordination the unload path does not honour. The jobs.busy() check is also a check-then-act across an await, though in practice _pipe is cleared in the first microseconds of the unload thread, so a job accepted in that window just reloads rather than failing.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Click 'Load model', realise it was the wrong checkpoint, click Unload. The request does not answer for the remaining two to five minutes of from_pretrained (it is parked on backend._lock inside a default-executor thread), the status dot walks loading -> ready -> unloaded as the two coroutines resume in that order, and the completed load is discarded. There is no way to abort a load; the button that looks like the way to do it is the slowest possible way of doing nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Refuse rather than block, the way a live job is refused, and close the check-then-act window at the same time: take _load_lock around the busy re-check and the unload, so the unload waits for a load at the coroutine level rather than inside a blocked thread and ensure_loaded cannot observe a half-unloaded backend. Aborting a load properly is a larger change and belongs behind a cancellation check inside load().

confirmed.title: The start-up menu's free-text repo-id sub-prompt spins forever at 100% CPU on EOF
confirmed.description: _pick's outer loop handles a closed stdin - `except EOFError: answer = ''` then an empty answer takes the default. The nested loop that reads a typed repo id has the same except and no exit for it: `while True: try: typed = ask('repo id: ').strip() except EOFError: typed = ''` then `if typed: return typed`. With stdin permanently at EOF the loop never terminates and never blocks; verified against launch._pick with an ask that answers once and raises EOFError thereafter, 200,001 iterations before the counter cut it off. clear.py records that this project already knows the hazard - 'isatty() is not a reliable signal here - it can report a terminal that has nothing to read - so let the read itself decide' - but configure() gates the menu on isatty alone and _pick's inner loop does not let the read decide anything.
confirmed.failure_scenario: `python -m backend.main` with no arguments on a terminal, pick the trailing 'another repo id' option, and then lose stdin - an SSH session that drops, a terminal window closed, a wsl.exe console detached, a tmux client killed. Reads then return EOF immediately and forever, and the server process burns one core spinning on input() without ever starting uvicorn. The user sees a listening-port-less process at 100% CPU that has to be killed by hand. On a real interactive terminal a single Ctrl-D is harmless, so this only bites when stdin is genuinely gone - which is also exactly when nobody is watching.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the inner loop the same escape the outer one has: an EOF at the repo-id prompt returns the default rather than re-prompting. A bare Enter still re-prompts, which is the intended behaviour; only a dead stdin falls through. A unit test in the style of tests/test_launch.py with an ask that raises EOFError after the first answer pins it.

confirmed.title: check_budget is per-image, so num_images multiplies straight past the only VRAM-shaped guard the API has
confirmed.description: check_budget() compares width * height against settings.max_pixels and ignores num_images. It is the one budget check on the request path - main.generate, main._expand for both grid routes, and generate.py all call it, and nothing else looks at the request's memory cost. num_images accepts 1-8 and is the field that decides how much is resident at once; CLAUDE.md states it plainly: 'num_images holds the whole batch in VRAM at once, runs hold one.' This is the previous review's unverified config.py:52 entry, unaddressed. In its favour, config.py does say max_pixels is 'set by the largest preset the UI offers rather than by what the GPU can take', so it was never claimed to be a VRAM budget - but nothing else is either.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified through HTTP against this checkout: `POST /api/generate {"prompt":"x","width":2048,"height":2048,"num_images":8}` returns 200 with a job id. 4,194,304 pixels passes the 4,300,000 budget, and the backend then calls the pipeline with num_images_per_prompt=8 - one forward pass holding eight 16,384-token sequences, on a card CLAUDE.md sizes at ~13 GB peak for a single 1 MP image on the fp8 path and 18.7 GiB for one 2 MP image with offload off. The UI offers both controls in the same panel (the 4 MP preset row and a batch input with max 8). The job ends in a CUDA OOM after a multi-minute weight load, or - under WDDM, more likely - spills into system RAM and limps, so a 64-cell grid takes hours to reveal it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Budget what the request actually asks the GPU to hold at once: add a second check on `width * height * num_images` against a new max_batch_pixels setting in config.py next to max_pixels, env-overridable, with a message that points at the axis that costs nothing ('use Runs instead of Batch'). All three call sites pick it up unchanged. Justify the number the way max_pixels is justified - the largest UI combination known to work - and say in the comment that it is a typo guard, not a VRAM model, since the real peak varies 2.5x by checkpoint and quantizer.

confirmed.title: The Origin allowlist always appends the port, so on KREA_PORT=80 the app 403s its own writes
confirmed.description: `_ALLOWED_ORIGINS = {f'http://{host}:{settings.port}' for host in settings.allowed_hosts}` builds origins by unconditionally appending the port. Browsers serialise an origin per RFC 6454 with the port omitted when it is the scheme default, so on port 80 the page at http://127.0.0.1/ sends `Origin: http://127.0.0.1`, which is not in the set, and block_cross_site_writes refuses it. The same shape breaks the documented KREA_ALLOWED_HOSTS LAN case behind a TLS proxy: the scheme is hard-coded http://, so an https:// origin is refused too. KREA_PORT is an advertised setting with no note that only non-default ports work.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified with TestClient: Origin http://127.0.0.1:7860 and http://localhost:7860 return 200; http://127.0.0.1 and null return 403; no Origin header returns 200. So `KREA_PORT=80 uv run python -m backend.main`, then opening http://127.0.0.1/, gives a page that loads and lists the gallery (GET is exempt) and then fails every write with 403 'cross-origin request refused' surfaced into the error slot: Generate, Run grid, Cancel, Unload, Favorite and Delete are all dead, and nothing in the message points at the port.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the origin the way a browser does - drop the default port and pick the scheme actually in use - or parse the incoming Origin with urlsplit and compare hostname against allowed_hosts and `(port or 80)` against settings.port, which also handles a proxy that terminates TLS. Add the port-80 case to the existing origin test, which only exercises the default 7860.

confirmed.title: torch and the Windows torchvision wheel are locked by URL with no hash, unlike all 103 other packages
confirmed.description: Every artifact in uv.lock carries a sha256 - 506 of them - except the ones from the PyTorch index configured in pyproject.toml. All three torch 2.13.0+cu130 wheels have no hash, and torchvision 0.28.0+cu130 has hashes for its two manylinux wheels and none for the win_amd64 wheel - the one this project installs on its primary platform. The recorded URLs also resolve to download-r2.pytorch.org, an object-store mirror, not the index host named in pyproject.toml. On both documented install paths (uv sync on Windows, wsl/setup.sh in WSL) the largest dependency in the tree - a ~3 GB wheel shipping native code loaded into the process - is fetched with the lockfile providing no integrity check at all. Pinning the version does not pin the bytes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A uv sync that fetches a substituted or corrupted torch/torchvision wheel is accepted silently; the lock cannot tell. Corruption shows up as an obscure import or CUDA failure hours later; substitution shows up not at all, and the wheel's native extension runs with the user's privileges the moment `import torch` executes, which wsl/setup.sh does immediately. Every other dependency in the tree, kernels and bitsandbytes included, is protected.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Re-run `uv lock` and check whether the hashes appear - if the index has started publishing them this fixes itself and the lock should be committed. If it still yields none, either source torch from PyPI (dropping the custom index) if the PyPI wheel's bundled CUDA now covers Blackwell sm_120, or pin the exact wheel URLs and verify them out of band once, recording the digests. Either way add a note under the README's install section that torch is the one unverified artifact, so the gap is known rather than invisible.

confirmed.title: Every failure raised while the lightbox is open is written into a slot the lightbox covers
confirmed.description: showError writes into #error, a paragraph inside the sticky panel at z-index 10; .lightbox is fixed, inset 0, 0.92-opaque, at z-index 50. So while the lightbox is up, #error is painted underneath it and is unreachable without closing the overlay. Three failure paths run only or mostly from inside the lightbox and report there: setFavorite's catch (the lightbox fav button and the f key), deleteImage's catch (the lightbox delete button and the Delete key), and loadGallery's catch, which stepLightbox awaits when an arrow key walks off the end of the loaded strip. Each returns early on failure, so nothing else changes on screen either: the star does not flip, the image stays, the strip does not grow.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two tabs on the same gallery - one of this app's ordinary states, since a job outlives its page. Delete an image in tab A, then in tab B open the lightbox on the same image and press Delete: the server answers 404 'unknown image', deleteImage returns, and the user sees an unchanged lightbox with no message at all. Pressing Delete again does the same. Likewise, after the server is restarted mid-session, arrowing past the end of the loaded strip fails silently and the lightbox simply stops advancing. Every one of these reads as 'the button is broken'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the overlay its own message slot and have showError mirror into it while the lightbox is open, clearing both on close; or promote #error to a fixed toast above the lightbox's z-index so one slot serves both.

confirmed.title: Activating Generate or Cancel from the keyboard destroys focus, because the control disables itself under the caret
confirmed.description: setBusy(true) sets `els.generate.disabled = on` on the button that was just activated; a disabled element cannot hold focus, so the browser moves focus to <body>. cancelJob does the same to its own button, and then setBusy(false) both re-disables Cancel and hides its container, so the focus loss happens twice on a cancelled run. Nothing anywhere restores focus - grep for focus() in app.js has no matches.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A keyboard user tabs to Generate, presses Enter, and their place in the document is gone: the next Tab starts from the Unload button in the topbar, seventeen stops from where they were. Combined with the absent live regions, the entire feedback for pressing the primary button is that focus vanished. Same on Cancel, where it happens mid-run and then again at done.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the pressed control focusable and mark it busy instead: replace disabled with aria-disabled=true plus the early return the click handler already has, and style [aria-disabled="true"] the way :disabled is styled today. If the buttons must stay truly disabled, move focus deliberately - focus Cancel after setBusy(true), and Generate from the done branch when activeElement is body.

confirmed.title: No prefers-reduced-motion handling: an indefinite blinking status dot and a full-page smooth scroll
confirmed.description: grep -rn prefers-reduced-motion web/ returns nothing. Two moving things run regardless of the setting: `.dot.loading { animation: pulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite }` with a 50% opacity keyframe blinks for the full duration of a weight load - CLAUDE.md puts that at several minutes - with no way to pause, stop or hide it, which is a WCAG 2.2.2 (level A) issue for blinking content lasting more than five seconds; and reuse() ends with `window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })`, an animated full-page scroll from wherever in the gallery the user clicked Reuse.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user who has set 'reduce motion' at the OS level still gets a dot blinking at 0.8 Hz for the whole of a multi-minute load, and a long animated page scroll every time they reuse settings from a gallery image far down the page.
confirmed.suggested_fix: One block at the end of style.css zeroing animation and transition durations and scroll-behavior under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, with `.dot.loading { animation: none; opacity: 0.8 }`; and in reuse(), pick the scroll behaviour at call time from matchMedia.

confirmed.title: 'Every official Krea/FLUX checkpoint is a gated repo' is false for the four klein entries, and the README says so itself 350 lines later
confirmed.description: README:19 opens One-time setup with 'Every official Krea/FLUX checkpoint is a gated HuggingFace repo. Log in first', followed by a table of three repos. The catalogue in launch.py carries four more, all marked gate='open' - FLUX.2-klein-4B, -9B, -base-4B and -base-9B - the start-up menu prints that word next to them, and README:366 states it outright: 'FLUX.2 [klein] (Apache 2.0 and not gated; the 9B and the undistilled -base- variants likewise)'. README:130 says the same of the lite-infer re-uploads the WSL path defaults to. Commit 4b96fbe added klein without revisiting the setup section.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A reader with no HuggingFace account, or one whose Krea-2-Turbo request is still pending, reads README:19 and the 'Access denied. This repository requires approval.' paragraph and concludes nothing runs until a human approves them. In fact 4 of the 7 checkpoints the menu offers - and every checkpoint the WSL path uses - need no login at all, and klein 4B is the cheapest thing here to try first (4 steps, 2.9 GiB peak per CLAUDE.md).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Reword README:19 to 'The Krea 2 and FLUX.1 checkpoints are gated HuggingFace repos; FLUX.2 [klein] and the lite-infer re-uploads are not. For a gated one, log in first:', and add the four klein rows to the table with gate 'open - no login'. A one-line pointer that klein needs no setup would let a new user get an image out before dealing with gates.

confirmed.title: launch.py restates config.py's three fallback defaults, and a bare-Enter menu writes them into the environment
confirmed.description: launch.py holds _DEFAULT_MODEL/_DEFAULT_QUANT/_DEFAULT_OFFLOAD, a second copy of Settings.model_id/quantization/offload. The comment gives a real reason for not importing config, but nothing checks that the two copies agree, and the menu does not merely display its default - configure() calls `os.environ.update(choice.environ())`, so whatever the menu resolves is written into KREA_MODEL_ID/KREA_QUANT/KREA_OFFLOAD and read back by the frozen Settings. The test suite cannot catch a one-sided change either: tests/test_launch.py asserts the same three literals from its own third copy, so editing config.py alone leaves all 135 tests passing.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Someone flips config.py's default checkpoint to krea/Krea-2-Turbo - the README already treats the default as a thing that moves; it was FLUX-vs-Turbo drift in the last review - and leaves launch.py naming FLUX. From then on `python -m backend.main --defaults` serves Turbo at 8 steps / CFG 0 / mu 1.15, while the same command bare on a terminal followed by three Enters exports KREA_MODEL_ID=FLUX and serves FLUX at 28 steps: two documented ways to start 'with the defaults' that now disagree, with the menu having printed FLUX as the marked default and given no sign anything was overridden.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Guard the copy rather than removing it. launch cannot import config, but a test can import both: assert the three launch defaults equal the three settings values under the clean_env fixture (config reads the environment at import, so the fixture's delenv must run first, or assert against the literals parsed out of config.py's os.getenv calls). Then drop the hard-coded literals from test_enter_three_times_keeps_the_shipped_defaults so it reads the same single source.

confirmed.title: generate.main() - the whole headless path - is never executed by a test
confirmed.description: `grep -rn 'from backend import generate' tests/` returns one hit, which reaches only generate._build_parser() to check that the CLI and the server share --model/--quant/--offload. The 250 lines of main() below it never run: _resolve_size's mutual exclusion, the gridding decision and the `seeds=args.grid_seeds if gridding else args.runs` mapping that turns --runs N into N grid cells, the --resume prune against completed_cells, the --dry-run early return, the per-image `wrap_seed(run_seed + offset)` and save_image loop, the SIGINT handler's two-stage cancel, and the `return 130 if saved < total_images else 0` exit code. None of it needs a GPU - _project() is already an injection seam and get_backend could be stubbed the way main.backend is. This matters because the CLI is the other writer into the same gallery, and CLAUDE.md's justification for duplicating the sweep loop ends with a promise - 'a cell in the browser and a cell in the terminal cannot drift apart' - currently kept by shared code alone, with no test behind it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Any change to the CLI sweep loop ships unverified. The concrete drift to fear is the seed maths: if the per-image wrap or the seeds mapping changed, an overnight `--runs 64 --batch 8` would write 512 rows whose recorded seeds no longer reproduce their images, and the only signal would be someone reusing one months later and getting a different picture. The browser path has test_a_sweep_reports_every_image_and_finishes guarding exactly this; the terminal path has nothing.
confirmed.suggested_fix: One test stubbing only the backend and asserting the cross-path invariant rather than the CLI's printing: `main(['a lighthouse', '--width', '256', '--height', '256', '--runs', '3', '--batch', '2', '--seed', '7'])` writes seeds 7..12 - the same six seeds the HTTP path produces for runs=3, num_images=2, seed=7. Add a --resume re-run asserting it saves nothing and returns 0. Three cautions: restore the SIGINT handler in a fixture (main() installs one and never removes it, leaking it into the rest of the session); do not assert on printed paths, since the store fixture patches storage.settings while generate.py prints from backend.config.settings; and put profile-derived assertions in a subprocess with KREA_* stripped from the environment, since settings is frozen at import.

confirmed.title: setup.sh installs uv into a PATH only it can see, then tells the user to run serve.sh in the same shell
confirmed.description: The install branch does `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` followed by `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` - and that export lives in the `bash wsl/setup.sh` subprocess and dies with it. uv's installer appends a line to the user's rc files, which only affects future shells. The script's own closing message then prints `source wsl/env.sh` and `bash wsl/serve.sh` with no mention of restarting the shell, and serve.sh is `set -euo pipefail` with `exec uv run ...`. This is the exact path setup.sh exists for: the fresh-WSL, uv-not-yet-installed case is the only branch that takes the install at all.
confirmed.failure_scenario: First run on a clean WSL 2 install: `bash wsl/setup.sh` completes with the CUDA check and prints 'Ready.', the user copies the two lines it printed, and `bash wsl/serve.sh` answers `wsl/serve.sh: line 10: uv: command not found` (exit 127). Nothing is broken - a new shell works - but the script's own success message hands the user a command that cannot run.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Track whether the install branch was taken and adjust the closing message: set a flag inside the if, and when set have the heredoc emit `. "$HOME/.local/bin/env"   # uv was just installed; this shell has not picked it up yet` above the source line.

confirmed.title: setup.sh tells the user to put the relative line `source wsl/env.sh` in ~/.bashrc, where it resolves against the shell's cwd
confirmed.description: The closing heredoc reads `source wsl/env.sh          # or put that line in ~/.bashrc`. wsl/env.sh is a path relative to the shell's working directory, and ~/.bashrc runs at shell start, where a WSL shell launched from the Start menu or Windows Terminal's default profile begins in $HOME, not in the repo. 'That line' therefore fails in exactly the shells the advice is aimed at. The heredoc delimiter is unquoted, so parameter expansion is already available, and setup.sh has already cd-ed to the repo root - an absolute path costs nothing.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user who follows the advice gets `bash: wsl/env.sh: No such file or directory` on every new shell. That is loud, but the state it leaves them in is silent and is the one README.md:135 calls out as destructive: with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT unset, the next `uv run` from the repo directory finds the Windows .venv, judges it broken and replaces it - losing the ~10 GB Windows environment.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Emit the absolute path the script already knows: `source $PWD/wsl/env.sh     # or put that line in ~/.bashrc`. Optionally note that exporting UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT from .bashrc also redirects uv in every other project on the machine.

confirmed.title: KREA_DEVICE=cpu skips the 'CUDA is not available' preflight and fails after the whole checkpoint has been downloaded
confirmed.description: The one cheap, legible guard in load() is `if settings.device == 'cuda' and not torch.cuda.is_available(): raise RuntimeError('CUDA is not available to PyTorch')`, and it fires before from_pretrained. But settings.device is only used on the offload == 'none' branch; the default offload == 'model' path calls `pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload()` with no device, which resolves its own accelerator and, in diffusers 0.40, raises 'enable_model_cpu_offload requires accelerator, but not found' when that is cpu. So KREA_DEVICE=cpu - the natural thing to try on a machine with no usable GPU - sails past the guard because the condition tests one exact spelling, downloads and materialises the whole checkpoint, and then dies on diffusers' message instead of the project's own. The --offload/--quant flags validate through argparse choices; KREA_DEVICE is read raw and validated nowhere. (A related lead: neither offload path is passed settings.device at all, so `cuda:1` silently loads onto cuda:0.)
confirmed.failure_scenario: No CUDA on the box. The user sets KREA_DEVICE=cpu and starts the server. It downloads ~32 GB and spends minutes loading, then answers a RuntimeError about a function the user never called, naming neither KREA_DEVICE nor KREA_OFFLOAD. Had they left KREA_DEVICE alone they would have got 'CUDA is not available to PyTorch' in under a second, before any download.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Preflight the device the run will actually use, not the one in the settings: compute `needs_cuda = settings.offload in ('model', 'sequential') or settings.device.startswith('cuda')` and raise a message that names both variables, and move the check above _quantization_config() so it and the Nunchaku preflight both run before anything is fetched.

confirmed.title: jobs.submit() re-implements grid.expand()'s seed loop, so the documented 'cannot drift apart' guarantee is not enforced - and they already disagree about the grid cap
confirmed.description: CLAUDE.md states: 'What it no longer duplicates is which images to make: both call grid.expand(), which with no axes set yields exactly the old runs loop ... so a cell in the browser and a cell in the terminal cannot drift apart.' That is false for the server's plain path. generate.py calls `grid.expand(request, ..., seeds=args.runs)`, but jobs.submit() builds the cells inline with its own copy of the arithmetic. The seed maths matches expand()'s today, but nothing enforces it, and one guard is already missing: expand raises past settings.max_grid_images, submit checks nothing. Verified with KREA_MAX_GRID_IMAGES=100: `backend.generate "a dog" --runs 64 --batch 4` exits 2 with '256 images is past the 100 a grid may queue', while JobManager.submit with the same request returns a job with 64 cells and 256 images.
