confirmed.failure_scenario: Today: a user who lowers KREA_MAX_GRID_IMAGES - documented as 'the most images one grid search may queue' - gets the cap enforced from the terminal and silently ignored from the browser's Runs box. Latent and worse: the seed-range bug already on this list (_MAX_SWEEP_SPAN not covering a grid's seed axis) will naturally be fixed inside grid.expand, and that fix will not reach /api/generate, because the browser's plain sweep never goes through expand. The CLAUDE.md sentence is what would tell the next reader not to check.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make submit() a thin wrapper over the shared expansion - `cells = grid.expand(request, seeds=request.runs)` - so the claim becomes true by construction. expand already forces runs=1 on each cell request and produces the identical seed sequence, so the recorded rows are unchanged; the only visible differences are a per-cell label (which showCell already renders usefully) and max_grid_images now applying to runs x num_images, which is what the README already promises. If that is not wanted, correct the CLAUDE.md bullet to say the two paths keep separate copies of the seed arithmetic and name jobs.py:141 as the second one.

confirmed.title: A fractional bound or step on an integer axis escapes the labelled error path and surfaces raw Python text
confirmed.description: parse_axis wraps its single-value cast in a try/except that produces the user-facing message, but the range branch three lines above calls _range_values(match, cast, label) outside any handler. The _RANGE regex matches `\d+(?:\.\d+)?` for start, stop and step, so a decimal is accepted by the regex and then handed to int(). tests/test_grid.py parametrises the bad-axis cases as ['12-6', '6-12x0', '6-12x-2', 'eight', '6..12'] - every neighbour of this case, but not this case - and only asserts pytest.raises(ValueError), so it would not catch the difference anyway.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: `grid.parse_axis('6-12x0.5', int, label='steps')` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '0.5'`, where `grid.parse_axis('8.5', int, label='steps')` correctly raises `steps: '8.5' is not a number`. Typing `6-12x0.5` in the grid Steps box - a natural mistake, since the CFG and mu boxes directly beneath take exactly that syntax and their placeholders are `0,0.5,1` and `none,1.15` - puts the bare Python message in the red hint under the grid panel, naming neither the field nor the spec that produced it, on a panel with three axis boxes. `--grid-steps 6-12x0.5` prints the same string to stderr.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Move the range call inside the existing handler (re-raising an already-labelled ValueError and otherwise wrapping it as `{label}: {token!r} is not a whole-number range`), and add '6-12x0.5' and '6.5-12' to the parametrisation, tightening it to `pytest.raises(ValueError, match='steps:')`.

confirmed.title: settings.outputs_dir.mkdir() at import time defeats clear.py --dry-run's 'nothing changed', and generate.py --dry-run --resume still creates krea.db
confirmed.description: config.py runs `settings.outputs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` as an import side effect. clear.py imports backend.config before it has parsed a single argument, and then goes to some trouble not to create the database it is reporting on ('A dry run reports; it does not create the database it is reporting on') before printing 'Dry run - nothing changed.' Separately, generate.py calls storage.init_db() inside its `if args.resume:` block, which sits before the --dry-run early return. This is the previous review's disputed clear.py:63 entry fixed only on the database half; the directory half, and generate.py's copy of the same mistake, were not addressed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified with a fresh empty directory: `KREA_OUTPUTS_DIR=$S/out KREA_DB_PATH=$S/krea.db python -m backend.clear --dry-run` prints 'Nothing to clear.' and $S/out now exists; and `python -m backend.generate 'a dog' --dry-run --resume --seed 1 --grid-steps 8,10` prints 'Dry run - nothing generated.' and leaves a 40 KB krea.db plus the outputs directory behind. Small on a fresh checkout; worse when the path is deliberate - `KREA_OUTPUTS_DIR=/mnt/photos/krea python -m backend.clear --dry-run` against an unmounted or misspelled path silently creates the mount point as a plain directory, which is exactly the state that later hides the real data behind an empty mount.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Move the mkdir out of import - a storage.ensure_outputs_dir() called from init_db() and from save_image before the first write, which is cheap with exist_ok=True - and delete the config.py line. Then move generate.py's --dry-run early return above the resume block, or guard it with `if args.resume and not args.dry_run:` - a dry run can still report the resolved grid without a database to subtract from, which is what it already does when none exists.

confirmed.title: hints_for() takes the live cfg_threshold but not the live negative_prompt_supported, so the CFG tooltip can promise a negative prompt on a checkpoint whose field is greyed out
confirmed.description: /api/status merges two facts from the loaded pipeline over the id-based guess - cfg_threshold and negative_prompt_supported - then passes only the first into hints_for(). hints_for overrides values['cfg_threshold'] and nothing else, so every hint string is formatted from the profile's negative_prompt_supported, not the merged one. Three of the five profiles' CFG hints assert something about the negative prompt: the flux entry says 'A real uncond pass - and with it the negative prompt - only starts above {cfg_threshold}', and _FALLBACK says 'Above {cfg_threshold} the negative prompt applies'. Both profiles carry negative_prompt_supported True. Meanwhile the UI greys the field off the merged value. The module's own docstring says the field exists 'rather than promising an effect that cannot happen', and CLAUDE.md gives the same reason for the threshold merge - 'the tooltip and the greyed-out negative prompt field cannot disagree'. For this half of the pair they can.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Point KREA_MODEL_ID at any checkpoint the substring table does not recognise as klein but whose pipeline has no negative_prompt parameter - a local directory (D:/models/flux2-4b matches 'flux'), a community re-upload, or anything falling through to _FALLBACK. The panel shows the Negative prompt box disabled with the note '(this checkpoint takes no negative prompt)' while the help badge one row down says 'Above 1 the negative prompt applies, at roughly 2x the time per step.' The user raises CFG to 3.5 expecting the box to enable, and it does not.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give hints_for the second override and let the text branch on it: `hints_for(model_id, cfg_threshold=None, negative_prompt_supported=None)`, applying both into values the way the threshold is applied today, with main.status() passing both merged values. Then either add a second guidance_scale hint per profile keyed on the flag, or append the klein-style clause and strip the 'and with it the negative prompt' clause when the merged flag is False.

confirmed.title: aria-label on the ten ? help badges replaces the tooltip text, so all per-checkpoint guidance is announced as a two-word title and nothing more
confirmed.description: Every help affordance is `?...` - ten of them. aria-label supplies the accessible name and stops the subtree being traversed for it, so a keyboard user tabbing onto the badge hears 'About steps, note' and never the sentence inside. The tip is also display:none until hover/focus, and it is not associated with the control it explains by aria-describedby - focusing the Steps input announces nothing at all. This matters more here than in a generic app: applyHints writes the checkpoint-specific text into the steps, cfg and mu tips on every status poll, and model_defaults' whole hints block exists so that 'what steps, CFG and mu mean on this checkpoint' reaches the user.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A keyboard or screen-reader user runs FLUX.1 Krea dev at Turbo's 8 steps, or types seed:42 into the search box having no way to learn the syntax, because the ten places that explain the app are announced only by their titles. The same is true of the grid-variable syntax, the range syntax, Resume's 'needs the Seed field filled in' and the entire key:value search grammar - none of which is documented anywhere else in the app.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Drop the aria-label from each .help span (or make it a plain 'Help'), give every .tip an id, and point the control it describes at it with aria-describedby - which reads hidden text, so the display:none styling can stay exactly as it is. Add :focus-within alongside :focus so the tip stays open while a link or the tip itself takes focus.

disputed.title: lifespan's synchronous backend.unload() - split on severity and reachability, not on existence
disputed.description: Both lenses agree on the mechanism: lifespan calls backend.unload() on the event loop, unload() takes the lock load() holds for its whole body, and the loop is therefore frozen for the remainder of an in-flight load. They split on how bad it is. The confirming lens traced the whole path, including uvicorn's `if not self.force_exit` gate that makes a second Ctrl-C useless once lifespan has been entered, and rated it MEDIUM; the disputing lens noted that with any client connection open uvicorn prints 'Waiting for connections to close' first and force_exit lands before lifespan is reached, so the hang needs a load in flight and no open connection - KREA_PRELOAD, a curl-triggered load, or a tab closed mid-load - and rated it LOW. It is reported in full as a confirmed MEDIUM finding at backend/main.py:93; the split is over exposure.
disputed.failure_scenario: See the confirmed entry. The disputed narrowing is that a browser tab left open on the page changes the failure from 'frozen loop, no output, no exit' to uvicorn's own drain path, which the separate Ctrl-C-during-a-sweep finding then covers.
disputed.suggested_fix: `await asyncio.to_thread(backend.unload)` settles the loop-blocking half either way and is one line; skipping the unload entirely while _load_state is 'loading' settles the rest, since the process is exiting and the OS reclaims the VRAM.

disputed.title: A failed PNG encode leaving a .png.part - split on whether the encode can fail without cleaning up
disputed.description: The two lenses agree that a hard kill mid-encode leaks a .png.part that nothing collects, and that is reported as a confirmed LOW finding. They split on the ENOSPC framing: the disputing lens verified against the installed Pillow 12.x that `Image.save` already removes a file it created when the encoder raises Exception, so a disk-full or I/O error leaves no partial and no truncated PNG - which also kills the proposed `Image.verify()` sweep as an unbounded read for a condition that cannot arise. What survives is the KeyboardInterrupt path: BaseException, so Pillow's own `except Exception` misses it, and generate.py's second Ctrl-C raises exactly that on the thread calling save_image, which then prints 'Forced stop.' and exits 0 with the partial left behind.
disputed.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C twice during a 4 MP encode from the CLI, or a SIGKILL / power cut at the same moment: a multi-megabyte .png.part that summarise() does not count and clear.py cannot remove. The ENOSPC variant, as originally filed, does not occur.
disputed.suggested_fix: Move image.save inside the existing try - correct either way, since storage's handler catches BaseException where Pillow's does not - and add the stale-partial sweep and count described in the confirmed entry. Do not add the Image.verify() pass.

disputed.title: The grid preview has no request-ordering guard, so a stale expansion can overwrite the current one
disputed.description: schedulePreview() debounces by 250 ms and previewGrid() then writes the response into els.gridPreview unconditionally - no token, no in-flight check, no AbortController - while the same file solves exactly this for the gallery with galleryEpoch. Two previews can be in flight at once. The lenses split on whether the responses can actually overtake each other: preview_grid does the expensive part synchronously and then awaits `asyncio.to_thread(storage.step_cost_ms, ...)`, which is a real yield point, so a slow request that got in first can hand off and be overtaken by a fast one behind it - but only across that one suspension, so the window is narrower than the finding's framing implies. previewGrid is also wired directly to the grid section's toggle event, which can fire while a debounced call is already out.
disputed.failure_scenario: Type `1-64` into the grid Steps box with Resume ticked (a 64-value expansion plus a completed_cells lookup), then narrow it to `8` before the first reply lands. The cheap preview returns first and prints '1 image'; the expensive one returns second and overwrites it with '1024 images - about 8h'. The panel then describes a grid the boxes no longer contain, and stale error text behaves the same way - a 422 for a spec that has since been fixed lands on top of a valid one.
disputed.suggested_fix: Give the preview the same epoch token the gallery has: capture `const epoch = ++previewEpoch` before the await and return early in both the success and the catch paths when it no longer matches. An AbortController stored module-level works too and additionally stops the server doing an expansion nobody will read.

improvements.title: Nothing says what happened to last night's run: /api/jobs hides every finished job, and no run history survives a restart
improvements.description: active_jobs() returns only jobs.active(), which excludes every terminal job, and resumeActiveJob() - its one consumer - silently does nothing when the list is empty. So the morning after, the page shows an idle Generate button and a gallery with 299 images in it, and nothing anywhere says the 480-cell grid stopped at cell 300, when, or why. The error string exists on the Job and the object is still in _jobs (up to 200 are kept) - it is simply never served; after a restart even that is gone, though every image carries job_id and created_at. A load failure does survive a reload, because _load_state is server-side; a generation failure has no such path. Two mechanisms, both small: a `storage.runs()` GROUP BY over job_id behind a GET /api/runs, surfaced as a Runs selector in the gallery head that sets `job:<id>` and switches to the sheet; and an `include_finished` flag on /api/jobs so resumeActiveJob can report the newest terminal outcome when nothing is live. Also show created_at in the lightbox meta line - the one served field the UI never displays, and the one that answers 'what time did it stop'.
improvements.caveat: Judges cut this to its cheap form. The banner is in-memory, so it answers 'why' only while the failing server is still up; the DB half answers 'how many and when' but never 'why'. A job_id-keyed Runs list splits a resumed grid into two rows and two partial sheets, so it wants the run_id from the resumed-night defect first. Mechanically: /api/jobs deliberately strips `images`, so take the run/total_runs counters, not images.length; do not reattach streamJob to a terminal job to get the message for free (its handler would dump all 299 images into the viewer on every page load); gate the banner so a three-day-old OOM is not re-announced on every reload; and use MIN(model_id) with the other aggregates, since SQLite's bare-column rule is undefined there. Fix the 'cancelled' terminal-status defect first, or the new banner will misreport a finished run.

improvements.title: The lightbox cannot zoom, so the comparison an overnight grid exists to make cannot be made in the app
improvements.description: `.lightbox img { max-width: 92vw; max-height: 78vh; object-fit: contain }` is the whole image display, and renderLightbox just swaps src. A 2048-square image is therefore always shown at roughly 800 px - 40% scale - with no zoom, no pan and no 1:1; the sheet is worse by design at 96 px with object-fit: cover. A steps or mu sweep is a question about fine detail (hands, text, texture, over-sharpening), and at 40% every cell looks the same, so the only way to answer it is to leave the app for an external viewer, losing the captions, the star and the arrow-key strip. A pure web/ change: wrap #lb-img in a stage, drive it with transform, and - the load-bearing part - do not reset zoom and pan in renderLightbox when the next record has the same size, so stepping with the arrow keys compares the identical crop at the identical magnification across cells.
improvements.caveat: Judges flagged four mechanics that decide whether it feels broken. The stage must be `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` rather than a hard 92vw/78vh, or flex shrinking plus overflow: hidden clips the fit view. A full-size stage swallows the backdrop click that currently closes the lightbox, so decide that behaviour explicitly. '1:1' must divide by devicePixelRatio, or Windows display scaling makes it a 1.25-1.5x resample - precisely the smoothing a sharpening sweep is trying to judge. The wheel handler must be non-passive. And the new Z/0 keys must sit below the existing `input, textarea` guard, since focus is never moved into the lightbox. Nearer 100 lines than the estimated 60, with no frontend test suite to catch a regression.

improvements.title: CLI grids print a cell count but no time estimate, though storage.step_cost_ms already exists and the browser preview uses it
improvements.description: POST /api/grid/preview computes `seconds` from step_cost_ms times the summed per-cell step count and the panel renders 'about 4h 12m'. The CLI's settings block ends at the cell count and the image count; there is no call to step_cost_ms anywhere in generate.py. So the one interface actually used for unattended overnight work is the one that will not tell you whether the run finishes before morning - and knowing a grid is fourteen hours is what makes you drop an axis before committing the night.
improvements.caveat: Do not add a third copy of the arithmetic: put it in one helper (`storage.estimate_seconds(...) -> float | None`) that both preview_grid and the CLI call, keeping the 'no rows, no estimate' rule. Add the model_id predicate step_cost_ms is missing at the same time, or a klein median (~1000 ms/step at 1 MP) prices a Turbo run (~1875 ms/step) at half - the CLI is exactly where --model changes per invocation. Guard the call with db_path.exists(), since step_cost_ms goes through _connect and would write the schema into any file it opens, and word the line as generation time rather than wall clock (the CLI pays a load every invocation). _duration also needs an hours branch: as written it renders a four-hour grid as '252m30s'.

improvements.title: No way to re-render a night's winners at full size, though every piece needed is already built
improvements.description: The documented workflow is: run a grid overnight at a cheap size, view it as a contact sheet, star the winners. There the trail ends - reuse(rec) restores one image's settings into the panel, one image at a time, and the user retypes the size and presses Generate. Twenty favourites is twenty manual round trips, and the clicking is the expensive half: it is where a seed gets mistyped and the image is not the one that was chosen. Every part exists: ImageRecord carries the complete reproduction set by design, submit_cells explicitly takes an already-expanded list of pipeline calls, `list_images(favorites_only=True, search='job:...')` returns exactly the set you want, and completed_cells keys on width/height so a 2K re-render never collides with the 1 MP grid it came from. A sibling of run_grid, roughly 30 lines.
improvements.caveat: Four gaps in the sketch. It must call check_budget() - 2816x2816 passes the schema and is 1.8x past the pixel budget, and both existing producers make that call. There is no 'current selection' in the UI and galleryRecords holds only the paged-in 48, so take the gallery's own filter server-side or fetch the matching ids first and put the count in the button. Dedupe with completed_cells + prune_done and 409 when nothing is left, the way /api/grid already does. Batch the lookup into one `WHERE id IN (...)`. And be honest about what it delivers: the pipeline draws latents at the requested shape, so the same seed at 4 MP is a new sample - the prompt and the sampling settings carry, the picture does not. For a prompt-variable grid that is the whole value; for a seeds-only grid the selection is thrown away entirely, so the hint must say the seed is kept for the record, not to reproduce the picture.

improvements.title: The scheduler stub never calls back, so DiffusersBackend's progress, cancel and per-image-generator code is executed by no test
improvements.description: StubPipeline accepts callback_on_step_end and never invokes it - it goes straight from retrieve_timesteps to returning images - and test_klein.py's stub does the same. Those two are the only things in the suite that ever drive the real DiffusersBackend.generate, so everything between the kwargs dict and the return is unexecuted: _step_end, which is simultaneously the only progress source and the only cancellation point; the per-image generator list the batch-reproducibility rule rests on; the silent unsupported-kwarg drop; and the 'model is not loaded' guard. Three lines in the stub (call the callback once per step) plus a small tests/test_backend.py - six assertions, measured at 1.05 s: progress reaches (5,5); should_cancel true after step 3 raises Cancelled having run exactly 3 steps; a cancel before the first step raises without entering the pipeline; the generators' initial_seed list is [99,100,101] for seed 99 batch 3; the result shape; and the unloaded RuntimeError.
improvements.caveat: One claimed benefit is overstated and must not be written into the test's docstring: a diffusers rename of callback_on_step_end is NOT caught, because the stub owns its own signature - the rename would leave the test green while the real Cancel button dies. Close that separately with a signature assertion against the real classes, which imports fine with no weights (verified for FluxPipeline, Krea2Pipeline and Flux2KleinPipeline) and also pins the assumptions behind cfg_threshold's three-way rule. Also note should_cancel is polled once before the pipeline is entered, so assert on the stub's own completed-step counter rather than the predicate's call count, and have the stub record the generator it is handed.

improvements.title: The prompt-variable assignment that made each image is thrown away, so a multi-variable prompt grid can never be laid out as a grid
improvements.description: Cell.variables is the exact assignment - {size: 'big', ground: 'dirt'} - that produced a cell, and nothing reads it: `grep -rn 'cell\.' backend/` finds only request, seed and label. save_image is handed the substituted request and stores only the finished prose, with no variables column and no key in the PNG krea block. Everything downstream then reconstructs it from strings: SHEET_AXES carries one flat prompt axis, so N variables crossed together collapse into a single axis of N-fold values - a 2x2 size-by-ground night renders as a 4-wide strip, never as the 2x2 it was - and promptLabels diffs word positions to recover labels, which fails outright on the `none` value the UI itself recommends. Persist the assignment (a variables TEXT column via _migrate, the job_id precedent) and make SHEET_AXES append one axis per variable name seen; chooseAxes then needs no change, since it already picks the two widest-varying.
improvements.caveat: Suppress the flat prompt axis whenever any record in view carries variables - do not merely keep it as a fallback, or chooseAxes will pick a 4-value prompt axis over a 2-value var axis and turn a single-variable run into a diagonal sheet. SHEET_AXES is a module const read in five places, so it has to be rebuilt at the top of renderSheet with the variable names folded into the layout signature, and _row_to_record needs the same `in row.keys()` tolerance mu and job_id already carry. renderSheet's prose() hardcodes `axis.key === 'prompt'` for header wrapping; variable values are prose too. Drop the `var:size=big` search term from scope - it needs a json_extract branch rather than the column+cast shape _FILTERS has - and note that sheetValues sorts strings with localeCompare, so per-variable axes render alphabetically rather than in declaration order.

improvements.title: FLUX.2 klein's reference-image conditioning is already loaded and completely unreachable
improvements.description: Flux2KleinPipeline.__call__ takes `image` as its first parameter, resizes each reference to <=1 MP, VAE-encodes it and concatenates the tokens onto the latent sequence every step. That is native multi-reference image editing - the FLUX.2 headline feature - at no extra weights, no second pipeline and no second download. The backend never passes it: _call_params already contains 'image' when klein is loaded, describe() already publishes derived capabilities off that same set, and the kwargs dict is exactly where it would go. GenerateRequest has no field for it and web/ has no control; the nearest thing is reuse(), which copies settings and never pixels. Reference a gallery image rather than building an upload path - smaller, and reproducible.
improvements.caveat: Cost is understated: a 1 MP reference roughly doubles the sequence and roughly quadruples the attention term, so expect 2-3x per image, not 'one VAE encode' (absolute numbers stay fine; klein-base at 50 steps with an uncond pass doubles it again). Joining a raw request string onto outputs_dir is an arbitrary-file read reachable from POST /api/generate - resolve it through the images table instead. `from PIL.Image import Image` in that module is the class, not the module, so the open needs a local import. The capability must be published like negative_prompt_supported (describe() plus the /api/status merge) and refused at submit, not discovered at cell 1 of a 64-cell night. Most importantly, reference has to enter grid.CellKey and completed_cells, or a resumed reference grid treats earlier text-only images at identical settings as done. Add --reference to generate.py in the same change, and note that validating against the gallery means only images this tool generated can be referenced.

improvements.title: An overnight grid started from the browser leaves nothing in the log, and no job carries a timestamp
improvements.description: The server logs a job only when it breaks - one log.error and one log.info about cancellation are the only job-level log calls in backend/. There is no line at job start, none per cell, none per image, none at completion. The CLI, for exactly this case, prints one line per cell when stdout is not a tty, a path per saved image and a closing total; the browser path - the one with the grid panel and the resume checkbox, i.e. the documented way to run a night - is silent. Job also has no timestamps at all, so GET /api/jobs cannot distinguish a sweep that is progressing from one wedged on a hung load. Four small edits: queued_at/started_at/finished_at in snapshot(), a line at job start with the cell count and size, the CLI's own per-cell line at the same point in _generate, and a closing line from the new timestamps.
improvements.caveat: Timestamps must be JSON-native floats (time.time()), never datetime - snapshot() is serialised by a bare json.dumps on the SSE path, which would raise mid-job. Set finished_at inside _finish(), not at the tail of _run: a job cancelled while queued never reaches that tail, and _finish is the one exactly-once terminal path. _run has no local `req` (it is job.request), and do not log a step count there - total_steps is the cell's, not the job's. started_at alone does not answer 'is it moving'; add a last_progress_at touched in on_progress. Drop the UI ETA from this change, and drop KREA_LOG_FILE - `bash wsl/serve.sh > server.log 2>&1` already captures these lines.

improvements.title: The grid spec lives only in the DOM, so Resume - the feature built for a dead night - needs the whole grid retyped from memory
improvements.description: There is no localStorage or sessionStorage anywhere in web/. The prompt, the prompt-variable block, the three axis fields, the seed count, the seed, the size and batch/runs exist only as input values, and the init block starts from the static HTML every time. Nothing server-side holds them either. README documents Resume as 'tick it and re-submit the same grid', and the schema refuses a resume without an explicit seed - so continuing last night requires reproducing, by hand and exactly, a variable block, three axis strings and a seed that is only recoverable by reusing an image of the run. Any interruption that outlives the tab - browser restart, reboot, closing the laptop lid - costs the grid definition, and retyping one axis slightly differently produces a different grid that resume cannot match, silently re-rendering cells.
improvements.caveat: Two-phase restore: the model-independent fields synchronously at init (ahead of buildPresets/syncSize/syncCfg/syncRuns so those light up from the restored values), and steps/CFG/mu inside applyDefaults gated on the stored model_id matching /api/status's - the id is not known until that reply lands, which can be minutes behind a load. Hooking the existing input listeners misses most writes: choose(), reuse() and the dice button assign .value programmatically, so put a debounced save inside the sync functions plus one delegated listener on the panel. Version the key, wrap every access in try/catch, and do not persist the Resume checkbox - a box that comes back ticked the next evening silently skips cells on a grid the user did not mean to continue. Drop 'open the UI from another machine' from the benefit: localStorage is per-browser and per-origin. Keep the 'recall the last 5 submitted grids' extra out of scope.

improvements.title: No --from-image: the PNG's own krea metadata block is write-only, so the CLI cannot re-run or vary an existing image
improvements.description: save_image writes a complete, machine-readable reproduction set into every PNG - prompt, negative, steps, CFG, mu, seed, model, job, size as a JSON text chunk, plus the A1111 parameters line - and nothing in the repo ever reads either one back (`grep -rn 'krea"\|\.text\[' backend/ tests/` finds only the write). The browser has Reuse from the database; the CLI has no equivalent from either source. So the nightly workflow that starts from an image you already have - 'that one at seed 7734429 was good, run four seeds either side at 2 MP' - costs a browser trip and six numbers retyped by hand, each a chance to get one digit wrong, at which point the sweep is comparing against a different image and nothing says so.
improvements.caveat: Placement is load-bearing: read the PNG before apply_env, not just before the GenerateRequest, or meta['model'] cannot fill KREA_MODEL_ID and --from-image on a Turbo PNG silently renders on FLUX while claiming to reproduce - the exact mismatch the flag exists to prevent. Use getattr(im, 'text', {}) (a JPEG has no such attribute) and meta.get('job') (that key postdates the others). meta['size'] is 'WxH', and the file's size can only win when all four size arguments are None, since _resolve_size cannot distinguish 'not given' from an explicit 1:1 at 1 MP. Do not inherit job_id from a --reuse <id> variant - display it, never reuse it. And land it with the --mu/--no-mu mutual-exclusion fix, since a third mu source makes that silent discard worse. The mu-is-null-means-no-shift point is already handled: main() always passes mu explicitly.

improvements.title: Deletion is all-or-nothing: no way to remove one bad night's images from the CLI, the API or the UI in fewer than N clicks
improvements.description: clear.py offers --yes, --keep-favorites and --dry-run, and clear_history is DELETE FROM images with an optional favorite = 0. The HTTP side has only one-row-at-a-time delete. Meanwhile the project already knows how to name a subset precisely - every image records its job_id and _split_search compiles `job:ab12cd seed:42 cfg:<=1` to SQL - and that machinery is read-only. A 200-cell grid started with a typo in the prompt, the case the whole resume/cancel design exists to survive, can only be removed by 200 confirmations or by destroying the entire gallery. The realistic outcome is leaving them in, which then poisons --resume and step_cost_ms.
improvements.caveat: Do not reuse the orphan sweep on the filtered path - a filtered clear that also removes every untracked PNG is a new all-or-nothing hazard inside the feature meant to remove one. Resolve to a concrete id list in one query and delete by id, chunked: it makes the count printed before the prompt provably the set that gets deleted, and prefer `DELETE ... RETURNING filename` so a row committed while the user was typing cannot be deleted without its file being collected. Accept only key:value terms and refuse leftover free text - list_images' LIKE fallback changes the predicate's semantics on any token with an odd quote, and a destructive filter resolved through a fuzzy index is not something to confirm blind. Note job: and model: are substring LIKEs, so the preview must name what it matched, not just a number. Keep the browser out of scope: the safety story here is the typed-'clear' ritual.

improvements.title: PNGs carry full metadata but nothing can read it back: no import, no reindex, and the WSL and Windows galleries can never be merged
improvements.description: save_image writes everything needed to rebuild a row and the filename carries the timestamp and seed, but Image.open appears nowhere in backend/. Everything an ImageRecord needs is recoverable - width/height from the image, created_at from the filename prefix, duration_ms 0 (inert, since its only consumer filters > 0), job_id from the metadata; only `favorite` is unrecoverable, because it is written to SQLite alone. Three consequences: krea.db is a single point of failure for an otherwise self-describing gallery; WSL and Windows keep deliberately separate indexes with no way to merge them; and a row whose file went missing can never be repaired. A backend/reindex.py in clear.py's shape - walk a directory, skip names already present (filename is UNIQUE, so it doubles as an idempotent reindex), insert through storage so the FTS trigger fires.
improvements.caveat: Read `Image.open(p).info['krea']`, not .text - .text is a property that calls load() and decodes every pixel (measured 5 ms vs 38 ms on a 2048-square PNG); the conclusion that no decode is needed is right, the API named does the opposite. Do not call the module backend/import.py: `from backend import import` is a SyntaxError, so a test cannot follow the house style. Copy into outputs_dir with the same .part-then-rename discipline (a half-copied *.png is exactly what the orphan sweep deletes) and compare against outputs_dir first so a reindex-in-place does not copy a file onto itself. Parse the filename prefix as UTC. _page orders id DESC, so a merged month lands above everything already there whatever its timestamps - walk in filename order and say so. Scope the A1111 fallback to this project's own writer or drop it, and say in the summary that favourites are not restored.

improvements.title: First run: the panel reads 'waiting for the job ahead...' for the whole multi-minute weight download, and there is no way to start a load from the UI
improvements.description: _run awaits _ensure_loaded() before taking the gate, and job.status is still 'queued' throughout, so the stream a client opens immediately after submit yields status 'queued' - which the client maps to 'waiting for the job ahead...' for the entire ~32 GB download. There is no job ahead; nothing is queued. The top bar meanwhile says 'loading weights...' from _load_state, so the page contradicts itself. Separately, POST /api/model/load exists and no UI element calls it: the header has only Unload, so the only way to start the first download is to queue an image, and the only way to retry after a gated-repo 403 is to queue another one. The very first thing a new user sees after their first Generate is a message saying they are queued behind work that does not exist, and the natural reaction - reload, or restart the server - is exactly wrong.
improvements.caveat: jobs.cancel() keys its immediate-finish path on `status == 'queued'`; introducing a 'loading' status without widening that to ('queued', 'loading') regresses Cancel-during-load from instant to a multi-minute no-op. Gate the label on whether a load is actually needed (`not backend.is_ready()`) or emit a second status event on the restore, or a job genuinely queued behind another gets the same mislabel inverted. The Load/Unload button pair is optional - Generate already retries a failed load and KREA_PRELOAD already pre-warms - and if it lands, decide deliberately what the button does while state is 'loading', since Unload mid-load is the separate blocking defect.

improvements.title: The grid's seed axis is a count of consecutive seeds, so you cannot sweep settings over the seeds you already know are good
improvements.description: expand() takes `seeds: int` and walks base + index * num_images; GridRequest.seeds is an int and --grid-seeds is type=int. Every other axis is a spec string through parse_axis, which already handles lists, ranges and de-duplication and already casts with int. Seeds are the one axis that cannot be given as a list - while the contact sheet already treats seed as a first-class axis it can put on rows or columns, so the display half is built and only the input half is missing. This is the second night of every two-night investigation: night one finds that seeds 4471 and 8823 gave the composition you want, and night two - those two seeds crossed with a finer CFG and step sweep - cannot be asked for.
improvements.caveat: Four small omissions in the sketch. expand()'s `total` multiplies by `seeds`, so replacing only the loop lets a 64-value list queue 64x past max_grid_images. `_resume_needs_a_fixed_seed` (and its CLI twin) tests `seed is None`, so a resume fixed by the axis but with a blank base seed is refused - the one case where resume is most clearly determinate. describe() takes the count and both call sites pass request.seeds. And do not wrap_seed a listed value: the schema's own ge/le is what turns a typo'd -5 into an error rather than a valid 9.2-quintillion seed. Also decide the cap deliberately (MAX_AXIS_VALUES is 64, seeds allows 256) and reword the comment that says stepping by num_images guarantees no two images share a seed - a literal list can overlap when num_images > 1.

improvements.title: On FLUX.1, real CFG is welded to the distilled guidance value, so a negative prompt cannot be used without also over-guiding
improvements.description: The backend sets both knobs from one number: guidance_scale is FLUX.1-dev's distilled conditioning value (3.5 recommended, and what the profile seeds) while true_cfg_scale is ordinary classifier-free guidance driving a second uncond pass. The app has one control, so the only reachable configurations are (3.5, off) and (g, g). The usual way to run true CFG on a dev-family FLUX - guidance embedding near 1.0 while real CFG does the work at 3-5 - cannot be expressed, and neither can 'keep the recommended 3.5 embedding, add a mild real CFG of 1.5'. The user types a negative prompt on the default checkpoint, leaves CFG at 3.5, and silently gets guidance stacked twice at double the time per step, with one column recording both values. CLAUDE.md states the mechanism correctly and then states the coupling as if it were the only option; that sentence is the design decision to revisit.
improvements.caveat: Wider than the sketch. /api/status cannot express the new state - cfg_threshold answers 1.0 for FLUX.1, klein and the fallback alike - so describe() needs a true_cfg_supported key merged the same way, and the two threshold consumers (the UI's greying, the CLI's '[ignored]' note) must compare against the effective true CFG rather than guidance_scale. The reproduction set is wider than ImageRecord: grid.cell_key and completed_cells' SELECT must both carry the column at the same rounding, plus the krea chunk, the A1111 line and a true_cfg: filter. FluxPipeline's do_true_cfg also requires a non-empty negative prompt, so the new value must stay gated on one or the row records a real CFG that never ran. Store the requested value with NULL meaning 'followed guidance_scale', mirroring mu. Ship the fourth grid axis as a follow-up - it is fifteen more touch points.

improvements.title: The browser can hold exactly one job, so the server's queue - built, tested and reachable from curl - cannot be used from the UI
improvements.description: startJob opens with `if (busy) return;` and setBusy(true) disables both Generate and Run grid for the life of the job, so the browser can never have two jobs in flight. The server was written for exactly that: submit/submit_cells create the task immediately and it waits on _gate; cancel() finishes a queued job on the spot 'so cancelling it does not first require the job ahead of it to end'; busy() is deliberately wider than _gate.locked(); and /api/jobs returns every non-terminal job while resumeActiveJob indexes the last of them. The giveaway is the client's own 'waiting for the job ahead...' branch - a state the browser has no way to produce for itself, reachable only if someone queues a second job with curl. Anyone with two experiments in mind for a night can start one of them; the 4-hour grid finishes at 02:00 and the card idles until morning with the follow-up already typed into the panel.
improvements.caveat: Change resumeActiveJob to attach to the oldest non-terminal job, not the newest, before landing this - with a queue, a reload would otherwise show 'waiting' while the running sweep's progress is invisible. `if (busy) return` is also the only double-submit guard, so disable the button for the duration of the POST instead. Do not call setBusy(false) between chained jobs (it nulls currentJob and hides the bar): split 'a job is being watched' from 'anything is queued'. And fix the queued caption in the same change, since during a cold load the first job of a session is 'queued' with nothing ahead of it.

improvements.title: The contact sheet never shows which cells you starred, and crops every cell it is meant to be comparing
improvements.description: Morning triage works - opening a sheet cell hands the lightbox the whole sheet in reading order, so the arrow keys and `f` walk and star it - but the result of that pass is invisible where it would mean something: renderSheet builds each cell as sheet-cell or sheet-cell empty and never consults rec.favorite, though the star badge already exists for gallery cards. So an interrupted pass over 500 cells restarts blind, and afterwards the conclusion - which row and which column the keepers cluster in - exists only in the user's head or behind a favourites-filtered gallery that has lost the grid layout entirely. Second, `.sheet-cell img` is object-fit: cover, so every cell is centre-cropped to a square: on an 832x1216 portrait run the sheet compares the middle 68% of each frame and hides the composition at top and bottom, which on these models is exactly what a CFG or mu axis moves.
improvements.caveat: `.sheet-cell` has no position: relative, so sharing the card's ::after star would pile every badge at the top of the page. setFavorite's DOM loop selects `.card[data-id]` only, so sheet cells need a data-id and a widened selector - do not just call renderSheet() on toggle, which wipes and rebuilds up to 1024 img nodes and resets the horizontal scroll on every keypress of a fast star-through. Derive one aspect ratio for the whole grid rather than per cell (size is not a sheet axis, so a free-text search can mix sizes). Skip the per-cell hover star button, or it repeats the invisible-tab-stop defect at 1024 cells; the badge plus the lightbox's `f` delivers most of it. Expect rows ~46% taller once the crop goes.

improvements.title: created_at is recorded, indexed and never used: no date filter, no date shown anywhere
improvements.description: Every row carries created_at, there is an index on it, and it is served on every record - and nothing consumes it. _FILTERS has seed/steps/cfg/mu/model/job and no date key, list_images orders by id, and created_at appears nowhere in app.js: not on the card, not in the sheet cell, not in the lightbox meta line. So the only way to scope the gallery to one night is job:<id>, reachable only by finding a card from that run and clicking its (hover-only) sheet button - and NULL for every row written before that column existed. Two nights spent on the same prompt are indistinguishable except by scroll position, and the key:value box that answers every other question about an image cannot answer the most common one.
improvements.caveat: Implement it as a half-open range, not a LIKE prefix. The `cast is str` branch returns a substring LIKE before any comparison is reached, and a non-str cast partitions '2026-09-06' on its own hyphen into a BETWEEN that matches nothing. A prefix LIKE also cannot use the existing index. More importantly created_at is UTC: an overnight run crosses midnight in every timezone, so a literal date term silently misses the tail of the night it names - parse the term as a local date and convert to a UTC range, which also makes date:today and date:yesterday easy. The size filter suggested alongside is a separate change (w:/h: drop in for free; size:1024x1024 needs a two-column special case).

improvements.title: No content hash is recorded, so nothing can tell you an axis produced identical images
improvements.description: The metadata block and the images table record what was asked for and never anything about what came out, so the first question after a sweep - did this axis do anything? - is answerable only by eye over a 96 px grid. And it is not hypothetical: _placeholders unions the prompt and the negative prompt, so `negative_prompt = '{avoid}'` with three values is a legal 3-value axis; on FLUX.2 klein the pipeline has no negative_prompt at all, so those three cells run the same prompt, steps, seed and generator and produce three bit-identical PNGs while the preview reports '3 prompts' and triples the estimate. A sha256 of image.tobytes() truncated to 16 hex, stored in a content_hash column and the krea block, costs a few ms against a 4-24 s generation and makes '1024 images, 512 distinct - the mu axis changed nothing' free and exact.
improvements.caveat: Bit-determinism is an unverified premise and the whole feature rests on it: two identical-kwarg calls must produce identical pixels through quantized kernels with components moving devices mid-forward. Verify with one two-cell grid before adding the column. Drop the ImageStat.stddev half - a legitimately dark image has low stddev, so it is a false-positive generator with no defensible threshold. `dupes:` does not fit _FILTERS (it needs a GROUP BY ... HAVING subquery) and a global one is close to useless; scope the count per job_id, and note a plain `hash:` term does drop in for free. Fold image.mode and size into the digest. The higher-value companion is the preview-time check the proposal mentions last - the resolved axes plus the published capability flags already make 'the CFG axis does nothing on this checkpoint' available at submit.

improvements.title: Nothing coordinates the CLI with a running server: two processes race for one 16 GB card
improvements.description: generate.py constructs its own DiffusersBackend and loads a second copy of the weights into the same GPU, with no check that the server is up or holds a pipeline - no --remote, no port probe, no lock file. The two processes already share the SQLite gallery safely (WAL, per-process write lock, .part renames), so the database side of coexistence was thought through and the GPU side was not. The server holds ~8 GB reserved in torch's caching allocator after its first generation even under model offload, so a CLI sweep started against that spends minutes loading and then OOMs on the first step - exit 1, zero images, and the failure arrives long after the command that caused it. The user's own mental model, 'the CLI is the web app minus the web', actively invites this.
improvements.caveat: Scope to the probe and drop --remote, which is a separate large piece (profile defaults would have to come from /api/status, --model/--quant/--offload rejected, --resume routed through GridRequest, Ctrl-C mapped onto the cancel endpoint, terminal status mapped back onto four exit codes, and per-image paths that cannot be joined onto the local outputs_dir). Probe GET /api/status, not a raw socket: the model is deliberately not loaded at startup, so a listener alone is the ordinary harmless state and would false-alarm every time. Refuse only when state is ready or loading, name the checkpoint the server holds, treat a timeout as busy, and place the check after the --dry-run guard. The check is one-directional and blind across the WSL/Windows boundary, so word it as advisory - and give the refusal its own exit code, since the README pins the existing four.

improvements.title: No way to hand the GPU back mid-night: the only stop is a cancel that ends the run
improvements.description: A job is running or terminal. cancel() is the only brake and it ends the job - a resumed grid is a new job needing the spec retyped and an explicit base seed - and unload is refused while any job exists, including a queued one. So while a 480-cell grid is alive there is no operation in the app that gives the card back, even temporarily. The machinery for a hold is already there: _generate polls cancel_requested at the top of every cell, and by that point backend.generate() has returned, so between cells the only live reference to the pipeline is the backend's own. One person, one GPU: the card that is eight hours into a grid is also the card they want for twenty minutes, and today that costs the remainder of the night.
improvements.caveat: Judges recommend the cheap half only: pause at the cell boundary plus torch.cuda.empty_cache() returns nearly all VRAM under the documented model-offload default (diffusers has already moved the weights back to CPU by the end of __call__), with a seconds-long resume, no busy() change and no load/unload race. The full unload-while-paused design needs a worker-written acknowledgement (never the endpoint's flag) or an unload lands mid-denoise, plus _load_lock on unload_model, and it is only needed for KREA_OFFLOAD=none, which CLAUDE.md already says does not fit these checkpoints. Whatever lands, a bare Event.wait() deadlocks shutdown() and makes cancel() a no-op on a paused job, so both must set the event and _generate must re-check cancel_requested immediately after. Budget 100-150 lines across four files, not 40. Note also that a hold which neither empties the cache nor unloads frees nothing another process can use.

improvements.title: No LoRA loading, though all three checkpoint families in the catalogue ship a LoRA mixin
improvements.description: The loader builds a pipeline and goes straight to offload; nothing in backend/ or web/ mentions adapters. Yet in the installed diffusers 0.40 every family this project serves carries one - Krea2Pipeline, Flux2KleinPipeline and FluxPipeline all mix in a LoRA loader - so load_lora_weights, set_adapters and unload_lora_weights are on the object the backend already holds. Style and subject LoRAs are the main way a local generator becomes personal, and they are the one input class this app has no expression for at all: the user has a 200 MB LoRA on disk and the only way to use it is to stop using this project. The grid makes it more valuable than usual, since set_adapters' scale is a per-call setting and 'the same prompt at strength 0-1x0.2' is exactly the comparison a sweep is for.
improvements.caveat: It is an fp8/int8/bf16-path feature: NunchakuQuantizer is not trainable and its linear layers are not nn.Linear, so PEFT's injection will not match - refuse before the download, the way _nunchaku_preflight does. peft is a new dependency (pure Python, all transitive deps present). The 'adapters must precede enable_model_cpu_offload' constraint is false - diffusers strips and re-attaches the hooks around injection - so hot-swap on the live pipeline is both cheaper and safer than baking the set into load(), which would create a second load path driven from the job worker. set_adapters mutates pipeline state and is safe here only because generation is serialised through the one-thread pool; say so at the call site. Land the lora/lora_scale columns, the krea key and the completed_cells key in the same change as the first working generation - images rendered without recording which adapter made them corrupt Reuse and resume permanently. torchao + PEFT is the unverified part (weight-only leaves an nn.Linear, so the unmerged path should work; never merge on a quantized base).

improvements.title: No running surface reports gallery size or free space
improvements.description: The only disk accounting in the project, summarise(), lives inside the destructive tool: neither /api/status nor /api/jobs carries file count, bytes on disk or free space, so the browser never mentions that the gallery has become 40 GB, and GridPreview estimates a run's time but not its size. When the disk does fill, the night dies at the first image.save with ENOSPC and, per the cell-loop defect, abandons every remaining cell. A GET /api/health carrying summarise() plus shutil.disk_usage, and an estimated-bytes field on GridPreview taken from the same recent rows step_cost_ms samples, is the half that stops the night dying - the panel already promises 'about 6h20m'; 'about 5.1 GB, 2.0 GB free' is what it is missing.
improvements.caveat: Do not put summarise() on /api/status: the UI polls it every 3 s and summarise globs and stats every PNG, so at 10k files that is a full directory walk three times a second on the event loop. shutil.disk_usage is one syscall and is fine there; the file tally belongs on an on-demand endpoint, cached, dispatched through asyncio.to_thread. The GridPreview bytes estimate is the weakest third - step_cost_ms touches no filesystem, and PNG size varies with image content far more than duration does - so ship it as an optional field under the same 'no rows, no estimate' rule and drop it first if scope has to give. The filtered-delete half of this proposal is ranked separately.

improvements.title: Nothing can answer 'which settings actually produced my favourites'
improvements.description: The favourite flag exists only as a column and is queryable only one value at a time: tick the toggle, type steps:8, read the count badge, repeat. There is no aggregation anywhere in the project - no GROUP BY in storage.py, no stats route. The naive aggregate would also mislead, since counting favourites per setting rewards whichever setting you used most rather than the one that works; what is wanted is the keep rate, and every input for it is in the table. One query behind a `python -m backend.stats` in clear.py's shape: model_id, steps, guidance_scale, mu, made, kept, percent, HAVING made >= 5 so a lucky 1-of-1 does not take first place.
improvements.caveat: The all-time table is confounded and should be presented as the weaker mode: over months it rewards whichever settings were in use while the prompts happened to be good. Scope it to a job or a grid by default - grid.expand guarantees the settings axes were crossed against the same prompts and seeds within one night, which is what makes the number mean anything - and route --job through the existing key:value filter machinery rather than inventing a second grammar. Group on the same six-decimal rounding completed_cells uses, or one CFG splits into two buckets after a round trip through SQLite REAL. Include width/height in the grouping. Call the column 'starred', not 'kept': nothing records a rejection, so an untouched night reads 0% rather than unknown. Land the CLI alone; the /api/stats route and panel are what would make it medium.

improvements.title: The pipeline facts the UI and CLI hang off are asserted against hand-written stubs, never against the real diffusers classes
improvements.description: cfg_threshold() and negative_prompt_supported are derived entirely from inspect.signature(pipe.__call__), and _PROFILES hard-codes the same two answers per checkpoint id for the not-yet-loaded case. Everything that checks either is a signature someone wrote from the same belief - KleinLikePipeline, StubPipeline, FakeBackend. The real classes need neither weights nor a GPU. About 20 lines: parametrize over the five id-to-class pairs and assert the required kwargs are still a subset of each __call__, and that the profile's guess equals the backend's answer from the real signature. Verified green today: FLUX 1.0/True, Krea2 0.0/True, klein 1.0/False.
improvements.caveat: cfg_threshold returns None while _pipe is None, so the test must set a non-None sentinel as well as _call_params or every threshold assertion passes vacuously. The id-to-class mapping is an assumption the test cannot verify offline - the loader resolves the class from the repo's model_index.json - so say so in a comment rather than presenting it as a checked fact. And cost is not free: importing the four pipeline classes adds ~2 s to a 9 s suite. Optional at near-zero extra cost: assert the exact spellings (true_cfg_scale, negative_prompt) rather than only their presence.

improvements.title: The PNG metadata - the only copy of the reproduction set outside SQLite - is never read back by a test
improvements.description: save_image embeds an A1111 parameters chunk and a krea JSON blob carrying prompt, negative, steps, CFG, mu, seed, model, job and size. No test opens a saved PNG; the existing one checks only that the file exists and no .part is left behind. The dict is therefore maintained by hand against a schema that has already gained mu and job_id since it was written. The database is gitignored, lives wherever KREA_DB_PATH points and is deleted wholesale by clear.py; the PNG is what survives all of that, so if a field is renamed out of the block, a year of images quietly loses its reproduction set and the 'disk is right' assumption stops being true.
improvements.caveat: Write it as a key-set equality, not a presence check, so adding a field to the reproduction set forces an explicit decision about the PNG instead of passing silently. Two mechanical notes: test_gallery's helper accepts neither mu nor job_id, so use test_storage's keep() or extend it; and meta['size'] is built from the image, not the request, so assert it against the record's width/height (the helper makes a 16x16 image for a 256x256 request). A non-latin-1 case is unnecessary - Pillow's iTXt fallback already handles it.

improvements.title: Nothing joins the checkpoint catalogue to the profile table, so a new entry can fall through to the generic fallback and the menu will print those numbers as if they were the checkpoint's own
improvements.description: launch.CHECKPOINTS and model_defaults._PROFILES are two hand-maintained lists that have to agree, joined only by substring matching inside _profile_for. Nothing checks the join: tests/test_klein.py asserts four hard-coded ids and tests/test_launch.py never calls defaults_for at all. All 15 catalogue repos plus their lite variants resolve correctly today, so this is a coverage gap rather than a live bug - but the failure is silent in both directions, and Checkpoint.summary() renders defaults_for(self.repo) straight into the menu, so an entry that missed every token prints the fallback's '28 steps, CFG 3.5' in the same column and format as a real profile. The matching is fragile enough to trip easily: `krea/Krea2-Turbo` (same model, no dash) resolves to 28/3.5. Add `Checkpoint('Krea 3 Turbo', ...)` and forget the profile row and a distilled 4-step model runs at 28 steps and real guidance with the whole suite green.
improvements.caveat: Detect the fallback by identity, not by value: the flux profile is value-identical to _FALLBACK in every non-hints field, so the obvious inequality assertion fails on the shipped default for 3 of 15 parameters. Identity alone is also necessary but not sufficient - a hypothetical FLUX.3 entry matches the flux token and would be handed FLUX.1's numbers - so make the pinned per-entry expectations the primary check and drive them from CHECKPOINTS so an unlisted entry is a failure. Drop the '(unrecognised)' suffix on Checkpoint.summary(): once the test exists it can never fire for a catalogue entry, and the string would overrun the menu's fixed-width column.

improvements.title: A running sweep reports no elapsed time and no ETA, though every ingredient already exists
improvements.description: While a job runs the only progress text is a counter plus the cell label; Job.snapshot() carries step/total_steps/run/total_runs/label/images/error and no timestamp, so the server cannot supply one either. When the job ends, setBusy(false) clears the text and a clean `done` shows no summary at all, so a finished grid leaves the panel indistinguishable from an idle page. Everything needed is written and already used before the run starts: step_cost_ms measures ms/step from recent rows at that size, humanTime formats it, and the grid preview combines the two. At 03:00 on 'run 712/1024' the user has no way to tell whether the grid finishes at 06:00 or at noon - and the counter hides the case where the run has slowed, since 712/1024 looks like 70% whether the rest takes one hour or twelve.
improvements.caveat: Get the cost unit right: save_image stores duration_ms per image, so step_cost_ms is per-image-per-step while the job's own per-cell elapsed is a whole-cell cost - mixing them is a silent factor of num_images. Prefer the job's own finished-cell timings over step_cost_ms for the mid-run estimate: it needs no DB access from snapshot() (which runs on the event loop) and, unlike historical rows, it actually tracks the throttling this is meant to reveal. Stamp finished_at in _finish so a terminal job re-read later does not report idle wall-clock, and stamp a second timestamp when status flips to running, since construction time includes the queue wait and the multi-minute load. The done summary has nowhere to go as sketched - #progress-text is inside the element setBusy hides.

improvements.title: The step callback already receives the latents; a live preview would cost one small matmul per step
improvements.description: _step_end is handed cb_kwargs['latents'] on every step - all three pipelines default callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs to ['latents'] - and throws it away, forwarding only (step+1, total). The whole transport is already built and load-bearing: on_progress to the SSE fan-out to the browser. A real vae.decode per step is out of the question under model offload, but the standard linear approximation - a fixed [latent_channels x 3] matrix applied to the unpacked latent - gives a blurry but compositionally accurate thumbnail for microseconds and no device movement. A 50-step klein-base or 28-step FLUX render is 30-60 seconds of a bar with no picture behind it; seeing composition emerge at step 3 lets a bad prompt be cancelled in five seconds instead of a minute, and cancellation already lands within one step, so the two compose.
improvements.caveat: An exception out of _step_end unwinds the denoising loop - that is how Cancelled is implemented - so the whole preview block must sit in a try/except that logs once and disables itself for the rest of the job: a shape mismatch must cost a preview, not a 64-cell night. '_unpack_latents' is not one API: FLUX's is a 4-arg staticmethod, Krea2's a 3-arg instance method returning 5-D, and klein has none - only a variant needing latent_ids, which the callback cannot reach - so ship for FLUX.1 and Krea 2 only. Key the factor matrix on (VAE class, latent_channels), since FLUX.1's VAE is the generic AutoencoderKL that 4-channel SD VAEs also use, and match the matrix to each family's normalisation convention or the preview is a confidently wrong-coloured blur. The callback hands you x_t, not x_0, so scale by the scheduler's sigma or step 3 is still mostly noise. Do not widen ProgressFn; add a separate optional on_preview. The matrices cannot be validated in CI.

improvements.title: A run cannot be given a wall-clock budget, so the night is sized by hand from an estimate
improvements.description: _generate's cell loop breaks on exactly one condition, cancel_requested, and GridRequest has no notion of time. The only sizing instrument is the preview's estimate, which the user reverses by hand into axis values that fit the hours available. This is the one case CLAUDE.md deliberately engineered for and then left unreachable: seeds are the outermost loop specifically so that 'a night that ends early - a cancel, a crash, a power cut - has finished every parameter combination for the seeds it reached', and every listed way of ending early is an accident. Estimate high and the GPU idles from 04:00 to 08:00; estimate low and the sweep is still going when the machine is needed. With a budget you queue 2000 cells against 'stop by 07:00', take ~1400 cleanly finished and seed-complete, and resume the rest.
improvements.caveat: Value is contingent: this project has no other workload on a schedule, so it buys tidier sizing rather than a new capability. If built, skip the new terminal status - putting a state in Job without adding it to _TERMINAL means active()/busy() never let go and unload 409s for the rest of the session; setting cancel_requested at the deadline reuses the existing path and already reports something other than 'done'. Plumb the deadline through submit_cells, not job.request (GridRequest-only fields are dropped when cells are built). The break is at cell boundaries, so it means 'start no cell after', not 'stop at'. And the headline payoff silently does not happen if the grid was submitted with an empty seed box, since resume then refuses to continue it - warn, or require a fixed seed. Seven files plus tests: medium, not small.

improvements.title: A grid cannot be exported as one contact-sheet image
improvements.description: renderSheet lays a run out as the matrix that produced it, with axis headers and pinned selectors, but only as DOM. There is no export path anywhere - no download, no canvas, no toBlob in app.js, and no route that composites images. The one artefact worth keeping from a night, a single image with the axis labels burnt in, can only be a screenshot, which is capped at the viewport and drops the pinned-axis caption. What that costs is comparing tonight's sweep against one from three weeks ago, and a sweep's result being able to leave the machine as one thing.
improvements.caveat: Judges split on layer and settled on client-side (canvas + toBlob + a download link): a server route duplicates a layout contract the client already holds - especially the non-round-trippable prompt labels - and adds a POST surface for no gain. If it is built server-side anyway: composite in asyncio.to_thread, take ids only (never filenames), send a rectangular matrix with nulls rather than a dense list (renderSheet leaves holes), do not write the result into outputs_dir where clear.py's orphan sweep will destroy it, cap the cell count, and embed the reproduction data plus the pinned-axis caption - a bare composite would be the one image in the gallery that cannot be traced back to what made it. Note also that recovering a three-week-old sweep is already one job: search term, so the real gain is the portable file.

improvements.title: Dead state: _error is never set, three describe() keys have no reader, and Job.request is written but never read
improvements.description: self._error is initialised to None, assigned None again on a successful load, and published as describe()['detail'] - no code path ever gives it a value, because load failures are caught in main.ensure_loaded() and recorded in _load_state['detail'], which is what ModelStatus.detail actually serves. The 'backend' and 'pipeline' keys have no reader either. Separately, Job.request is never read - _generate uses cell.request and snapshot() omits it. The cost is a contract that is wider than it is: FakeBackend.describe() carries three keys nobody wants, 'detail' reads as the backend's error channel while the real one lives elsewhere, and the next backend author copies both.
improvements.caveat: 'Keep pipeline and log it once at load' is already done - the loader logs the resolved pipeline class on every load - so all three keys can simply go, or the class name can be folded into the existing 'model ready' line, which is the one of the three with real diagnostic value. Deleting keys alone does not deliver the stated benefit, since base.describe()'s docstring names none while main.status() hard-indexes model_id/quantization/offload and would 500 on a backend that omits one: name the required and optional keys in that docstring in the same change. Pair it with the mu row.keys() lead so the dead-state cleanups land as one pass.

improvements.title: clean_env leaks KREA_MODEL_ID/QUANT/OFFLOAD into the rest of the pytest session
improvements.description: clean_env calls monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False); when the variable is absent - the normal case - monkeypatch has nothing to record and restores nothing at teardown. launch.configure() and apply_env() then write into the real os.environ and those values outlive the test. Verified: appending a trivial assertion after tests/test_launch.py fails with KREA_MODEL_ID=krea/Krea-2-Turbo, alongside KREA_QUANT=fp8 and KREA_OFFLOAD=model. Harmless today only by luck and by one prior workaround - _settings_in_subprocess strips KREA_* by hand - so the next subprocess or fresh-interpreter test written the obvious way passes or fails depending on collection order.
improvements.caveat: Make clean_env a generator fixture with an explicit save/restore (it currently returns None with no yield). Keep the KREA_-stripping in _settings_in_subprocess regardless: wsl/env.sh exports these into the real shell, so a suite run after sourcing it needs that strip whether or not this leak exists. Optional unless the CLI test lands, in which case land them together.

unverified.title: Quantized and Nunchaku load paths force model_id through hf_hub_download, so a local checkpoint directory dies before the loader sees it
unverified.note: _hub_file() always calls hf_hub_download, which rejects anything that is not a Hub repo id, and two call sites run before the pipeline is constructed: _component_libraries (reached for fp8/int8) and _nunchaku_preflight. from_pretrained itself has no such restriction - it branches on os.path.isdir - so the same directory loads fine under --quant none and fails under the default fp8 with an HFValidationError naming the model id and not quantization. The obvious next move, --quant none, then OOMs on a 16 GB card. Fix: resolve locally in the one shared helper when the id is a directory.

unverified.title: save_image never recreates outputs_dir, the one directory the module does not self-heal
unverified.note: outputs_dir is created once, at import of config.py, and nowhere else; save_image writes straight into it with no check. The same module self-heals the equivalent condition for the database, with a comment explaining why. Nothing else notices either: Path.glob on a missing directory returns [] rather than raising, so summarise() reports 0 files and clear_history reports success while every generation fails. Delete or rename outputs/ while the server is up and the weights load, the full denoise runs, and it dies in save_image with FileNotFoundError; /outputs also stops serving, because the StaticFiles mount resolved the path at start-up. One line before the write fixes the write path and the mount for everything afterwards.

unverified.title: settings.device is ignored on both offload paths, and a `cuda:0` spelling slips past the CUDA preflight
unverified.note: Both accelerate calls are made with no device argument, so diffusers resolves its own accelerator and _offload_gpu_id defaults to 0: KREA_DEVICE=cuda:1 silently loads onto cuda:0 while describe() reports GPU 0's name and VRAM, so nothing on screen says the setting was dropped. The preflight is spelled as an equality test against 'cuda', so the natural cuda:0 skips it. Fix: pass settings.device to both offload calls, test `torch.device(...).type == 'cuda'`, and report the device actually in use. Undocumented setting, so the exposed population is small.

unverified.title: stepLightbox re-anchors on its own pre-await record, so a back-step during the page fetch is still discarded
unverified.note: The rewrite since da7f774 correctly handles the list mutating under the await, but `lbList.indexOf(current)` also overwrites any index change the user made during that window - the failure the original lead described. Reachable only at a page boundary on the gallery strip and only inside the fetch window: ArrowRight suspends in loadGallery, ArrowLeft (which awaits nothing) moves back synchronously, and the resuming call re-imposes its own start and steps forward, landing two images ahead of where the user asked. Fix: after the await, return early when `lbList[lbIndex] !== current` before re-anchoring.

unverified.title: The lightbox image is published as decorative (alt="") while the gallery and viewer set alt to the prompt
unverified.note: renderLightbox sets .src and never .alt, so the largest and most deliberately opened image in the app is removed from the accessibility tree while the same image in two smaller contexts is described. Less severe than filed - #lb-meta is rebuilt on every render and begins with the prompt - so this is a consistency defect rather than information loss. Fix: set els.lbImg.alt = rec.prompt beside the src and clear it on close. The larger gap in the same feature is the missing dialog semantics, reported as a confirmed finding.

unverified.title: --quiet still emits two non-path lines
unverified.note: The headline half was fixed by correcting the README to document the `<path>  seed <n>` form. Two other stdout writes are not gated on args.quiet: the --dry-run acknowledgement and the resume no-op message, both to stdout rather than stderr, so `... --resume --quiet > paths.txt` can write an English sentence into a file being read as a list of PNGs. generate.py's own --help is also stale ('only print saved filenames'). Fix: route both to stderr and correct the help text.

unverified.title: The size preset table is maintained in four places
unverified.note: The 15-entry aspect-by-tier table lives in generate.py and web/app.js (verified identical today, held only by a comment), config.py derives max_side and max_pixels from it in prose and then hard-codes 2816 and 4,300,000 (the table's actual maxima are 2736 and 4,205,568), and README prints a fourth copy. No test compares them. A UI-only change to a preset makes --resume unable to continue a browser grid, since completed_cells keys on width and height; an app.js-only new tier is rejected by the schema it posts to. Fix: one owner in backend/sizes.py with config deriving its ceilings, or at minimum a test that parses the JS constant and compares.

unverified.title: describe()'s detail/backend/pipeline keys reach no consumer, and the ABC's docstring invites a second backend to use them
unverified.note: Also filed as improvement 32. The specific risk worth recording as a lead: someone implementing the second backend CLAUDE.md invites sets describe()['detail'] on a failed connect, following the ABC docstring and the existing _error field as precedent, and the message never reaches the browser - main.py returns _load_state['detail'], which stays None whenever the failure did not raise out of backend.load(). Either delete the channel or make it real, and name the required keys in the docstring.

unverified.title: The mu read guard's comment describes a legacy database this project has never produced
unverified.note: `mu=row['mu'] if 'mu' in row.keys() else None` is justified by 'databases written before mu was indexed have no such column' - but mu has been in _SCHEMA since the commit that first added the app, and the guard dates to the commit that fixed ImageRecord not serving mu. Every record-building read is SELECT *, so the condition is always true. It now sits three lines above job_id, which has both a read guard and a real _migrate branch - so the file contains a worked example of the pattern it has itself rejected, and the next person to add a column may copy the read guard without the migration, at which point every INSERT fails on an older gallery. Fix: read mu directly and delete the comment.
